**Commentary on Surah al-Fath (The Victory)**

It is Meccan.

Imam Ahmad [[In T: "Al-Bukhari, Muslim and Imam Ahmad narrated."]] said: Waki' narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mughaffal say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited Surah al-Fath during his journey in the year of the Conquest (al-Fath), on his riding animal, and he trilled in it. Mu'awiyah said: "Were it not that I dislike people gathering around us, I would have imitated his recitation for you." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it through the hadith of Shu'bah with this chain [Al-Musnad (5/24), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4835), Sahih Muslim no. (794)].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

This noble surah was revealed when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from al-Hudaybiyyah in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the sixth year after the Hijrah (migration), when the polytheists prevented him from reaching the Sacred Mosque to perform his 'umrah (lesser pilgrimage) there, and stood between him and that. Then they inclined toward reconciliation and truce, and that he should return that year and come the following year. He agreed to this, though some of the Companions disliked it, among them Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), as its details will come in its place in the tafsir of this surah, Allah willing. When he slaughtered his hadi (sacrificial animal) where he had been prevented, and returned, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed this surah concerning what had occurred between him and them, and made that truce a victory (fath) in consideration of the benefit in it and the outcome to which the matter led. This is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) and others, that he said: "You count the victory as the Conquest of Makkah, but we count the victory as the Truce of al-Hudaybiyyah."

Al-A'mash narrated from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: "We did not count the victory except as the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah." [Narrated by al-Tabari (26/44).]

Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "You count the victory as the Conquest of Makkah, and the Conquest of Makkah was indeed a victory. But we count the victory as the Pledge of Ridwan on the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah. We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), fourteen hundred of us, and al-Hudaybiyyah was a well. We drew out all its water, and we left not a drop in it. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he came to it and sat on its edge, then called for a vessel of water and performed ablution, then rinsed his mouth and made supplication, then poured it into the well. We left it a short while, then it gave us water to drink, both us and our mounts, as much as we wished." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4150).]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nuh narrated to us, Malik ibn Anas narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father [[In T: "And Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain."]], from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey. I asked him about something three times, and he did not answer me. So I said to myself: 'May your mother lose you, O son of al-Khattab! You have pressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) three times and he has not answered you!' So I mounted my riding animal and went ahead, fearing that something had been revealed concerning me. Then suddenly I heard a caller calling: 'O Umar, where is Umar?' So I returned, thinking that something had been revealed concerning me. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'There has been revealed to me tonight [[In M: "There was revealed."]] [[In T, M: "last night."]] a surah more beloved to me than the world and what is in it: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your previous sin and what will follow﴾.'"

Al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it through various routes from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him [Al-Musnad (1/31), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4833), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3262), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11499)]. Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a Madinan chain [good] [[Addition from M.]], and we did not find it except with them."

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The verse ﴿that Allah may forgive you your previous sin and what will follow﴾ was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) on his return from al-Hudaybiyyah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'There has been revealed to me a verse more beloved to me than all that is upon the earth.' Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it to them, and they said: 'Congratulations (hanī'an marī'an), O Prophet of Allah! Allah has made clear what He will do with you, so what will He do with us?' Then there was revealed to him: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens﴾ until: ﴿a great attainment﴾ [al-Fath: 5]." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs through the narration of Qatadah [Al-Musnad (3/197), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4148), Sahih Muslim no. (1786)].

Imam Ahmad [[In T: "And narrated."]] said: Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, Mujammi' ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, who said: I heard my father narrate from his paternal uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Yazid al-Ansari, from his paternal uncle Mujammi' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, and he was one of the reciters who recited the Qur'an, who said: "We witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah, and when we turned back from it, people were driving the camels hard. The people said to one another: 'What is wrong with the people?' They said: 'Revelation has come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So we went out with the people, hastening. Suddenly the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was on his riding animal at Kara' al-Ghamim, and the people gathered around him, and he recited to them: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾. A man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and is this a victory?' He said: 'Yes, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, it is indeed a victory.'" Khaybar was then divided among the people of al-Hudaybiyyah, and no one entered with them in it except those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided it into eighteen shares, and the army was one thousand five hundred horsemen. He gave the horseman two shares and the foot soldier one share.

Abu Dawud narrated it in the Book of Jihad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mujammi' ibn Ya'qub, with this chain [Al-Musnad (3/420), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2736)].

Ibn Jarir [[In T: "And narrated."]] said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to us, Abu Bahr narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Jami' ibn Shaddad narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Alqamah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say [[In T: "From Ibn Mas'ud, who said."]]: "When we came back from al-Hudaybiyyah, we halted at night to rest and slept, and we did not wake up until the sun had risen. We woke up while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was still asleep. We said: 'Proceed' [[In M: "Be quiet."]]. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) woke up and said: 'Do what you used to do, and likewise whoever sleeps or forgets.'" He said: "We lost the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and searched for her, and we found her with her halter caught in a tree. I brought her to him, and he mounted her [[In T: "So he mounted."]]. While we were traveling, the revelation came to him. He said: when revelation came to him he was overwhelmed by it, and when it lifted from him, he told us that there had been revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾."

Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through more than one route, from Jami' ibn Shaddad with this chain [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/43), Al-Musnad (1/464), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (447), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (8853)].

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqah, who said: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah [[In T: "And Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain."]] say: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray until his feet swelled. It was said to him: 'Has not Allah forgiven you your previous sin and what will follow?' He said: 'Shall I not be a grateful servant?'"

Al-Bukhari and Muslim [[In T: "Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it."]], and the rest of the compilers except Abu Dawud, narrated it through the hadith of Ziyad with this chain [Al-Musnad (4/55), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4836), Sahih Muslim no. (2819), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (412), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/219), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1419)].

Imam Ahmad said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Abu Sakhr informed me, from Ibn Qusayt, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he prayed, would stand until his two feet cracked [[In A: "until his feet split."]]."

Aishah said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, do you do this when Allah has forgiven you your previous sin and what will follow?" He said: "O Aishah, shall I not be a grateful servant?"

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih through the narration of Abd Allah ibn Wahb, with this chain [Al-Musnad (6/115), Sahih Muslim no. (2820)].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Awn al-Kharraz narrated to us, and he was trustworthy in Makkah, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us [[In A: "Bashir."]], Mis'ar narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood (in prayer) until his feet swelled, or he said his shins [swelled]. It was said to him: 'Has not Allah forgiven you your previous sin and what will follow?' He said: 'Shall I not be a grateful servant?'" This is a strange (gharib) narration from this route [Abu Ya'la narrated it in his Musnad (5/280) through the route of Abd Allah ibn Awn al-Kharraz with this chain. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad no. (2380), Kashf al-Astar, through the route of al-Husayn ibn al-Aswad from Muhammad ibn Bishr with this chain, and al-Bazzar said: "We do not know anyone who narrated this hadith with this chain except al-Husayn ibn Bishr and Abd Allah ibn Awn al-Kharraz. Others have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Bishr, from Mis'ar, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, and this is the correct one." So al-Bazzar's statement here clarifies the words of al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir: "This is a strange narration from this route."]].

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾, meaning: manifest and evident. What is meant by it is the Truce of al-Hudaybiyyah, for through it there came about abundant good. People became secure, some of them mixed with others, a believer spoke with a disbeliever, and beneficial knowledge and faith spread.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that Allah may forgive you your previous sin and what will follow﴾: this is one of his special qualities (khasa'is), peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in which no one else shares. And it is not established for anyone else, in terms of the reward of deeds, that his previous and later sins are forgiven. This is a great honor for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in all his affairs was upon obedience, righteousness and steadfastness, which no human other than him has attained, neither among the earlier nor the later generations. He is the most perfect of humanity without qualification, and their master in this world and the Hereafter. Since he was the most obedient of Allah's creation to Allah, and the most mindful of honoring His commands and prohibitions, when the she-camel knelt with him, he said: "The one who stopped the elephant has stopped her" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (2731, 2732).]]. Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me today for anything by which they honor the sanctities of Allah except that I will grant them it." So when he obeyed Allah in that and agreed to the truce, Allah said to him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your previous sin and what will follow, and complete His favor upon you﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾, meaning: by what He prescribes for you of the great Law and the upright religion.

﴿And Allah will help you with a mighty help﴾, meaning: because of your submission to the command of Allah, Allah will elevate you and help you against your enemies, as came in the authentic hadith: "Allah does not increase a servant through pardon except in honor, and no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him" [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2588) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. And from Umar ibn al-Khattab [(may Allah be pleased with him)] [[Addition from T.]], that he said: "You will not punish anyone who disobeys Allah, the Exalted, concerning you [in this world and the Hereafter] with the like of obeying Allah concerning him."

* *

This noble surah was revealed when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from al-Hudaybiyyah in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the sixth year after the Hijrah (migration), when the polytheists prevented him from reaching the Sacred Mosque to perform his 'umrah (lesser pilgrimage) there, and stood between him and that. Then they inclined toward reconciliation and truce, and that he should return that year and come the following year. He agreed to this, though some of the Companions disliked it, among them Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), as its details will come in its place in the tafsir of this surah, Allah willing. When he slaughtered his hadi (sacrificial animal) where he had been prevented, and returned, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed this surah concerning what had occurred between him and them, and made that truce a victory (fath) in consideration of the benefit in it and the outcome to which the matter led. This is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) and others, that he said: "You count the victory as the Conquest of Makkah, but we count the victory as the Truce of al-Hudaybiyyah."

Al-A'mash narrated from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: "We did not count the victory except as the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah." [Narrated by al-Tabari (26/44).]

Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "You count the victory as the Conquest of Makkah, and the Conquest of Makkah was indeed a victory. But we count the victory as the Pledge of Ridwan on the Day of al-Hudaybiyyah. We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), fourteen hundred of us, and al-Hudaybiyyah was a well. We drew out all its water, and we left not a drop in it. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he came to it and sat on its edge, then called for a vessel of water and performed ablution, then rinsed his mouth and made supplication, then poured it into the well. We left it a short while, then it gave us water to drink, both us and our mounts, as much as we wished." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4150).]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nuh narrated to us, Malik ibn Anas narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father [[In T: "And Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain."]], from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on a journey. I asked him about something three times, and he did not answer me. So I said to myself: 'May your mother lose you, O son of al-Khattab! You have pressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) three times and he has not answered you!' So I mounted my riding animal and went ahead, fearing that something had been revealed concerning me. Then suddenly I heard a caller calling: 'O Umar, where is Umar?' So I returned, thinking that something had been revealed concerning me. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'There has been revealed to me tonight [[In M: "There was revealed."]] [[In T, M: "last night."]] a surah more beloved to me than the world and what is in it: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your previous sin and what will follow﴾.'"

Al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it through various routes from Malik, may Allah have mercy on him [Al-Musnad (1/31), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4833), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3262), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11499)]. Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a Madinan chain [good] [[Addition from M.]], and we did not find it except with them."

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The verse ﴿that Allah may forgive you your previous sin and what will follow﴾ was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) on his return from al-Hudaybiyyah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'There has been revealed to me a verse more beloved to me than all that is upon the earth.' Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it to them, and they said: 'Congratulations (hanī'an marī'an), O Prophet of Allah! Allah has made clear what He will do with you, so what will He do with us?' Then there was revealed to him: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens﴾ until: ﴿a great attainment﴾ [al-Fath: 5]." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs through the narration of Qatadah [Al-Musnad (3/197), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4148), Sahih Muslim no. (1786)].

Imam Ahmad [[In T: "And narrated."]] said: Ishaq ibn Isa narrated to us, Mujammi' ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, who said: I heard my father narrate from his paternal uncle Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Yazid al-Ansari, from his paternal uncle Mujammi' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, and he was one of the reciters who recited the Qur'an, who said: "We witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah, and when we turned back from it, people were driving the camels hard. The people said to one another: 'What is wrong with the people?' They said: 'Revelation has come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So we went out with the people, hastening. Suddenly the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was on his riding animal at Kara' al-Ghamim, and the people gathered around him, and he recited to them: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾. A man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and is this a victory?' He said: 'Yes, by Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, it is indeed a victory.'" Khaybar was then divided among the people of al-Hudaybiyyah, and no one entered with them in it except those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyyah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided it into eighteen shares, and the army was one thousand five hundred horsemen. He gave the horseman two shares and the foot soldier one share.

Abu Dawud narrated it in the Book of Jihad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mujammi' ibn Ya'qub, with this chain [Al-Musnad (3/420), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2736)].

Ibn Jarir [[In T: "And narrated."]] said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to us, Abu Bahr narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Jami' ibn Shaddad narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Alqamah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say [[In T: "From Ibn Mas'ud, who said."]]: "When we came back from al-Hudaybiyyah, we halted at night to rest and slept, and we did not wake up until the sun had risen. We woke up while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was still asleep. We said: 'Proceed' [[In M: "Be quiet."]]. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) woke up and said: 'Do what you used to do, and likewise whoever sleeps or forgets.'" He said: "We lost the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and searched for her, and we found her with her halter caught in a tree. I brought her to him, and he mounted her [[In T: "So he mounted."]]. While we were traveling, the revelation came to him. He said: when revelation came to him he was overwhelmed by it, and when it lifted from him, he told us that there had been revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾."

Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through more than one route, from Jami' ibn Shaddad with this chain [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/43), Al-Musnad (1/464), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (447), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (8853)].

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqah, who said: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah [[In T: "And Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain."]] say: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray until his feet swelled. It was said to him: 'Has not Allah forgiven you your previous sin and what will follow?' He said: 'Shall I not be a grateful servant?'"

Al-Bukhari and Muslim [[In T: "Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it."]], and the rest of the compilers except Abu Dawud, narrated it through the hadith of Ziyad with this chain [Al-Musnad (4/55), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4836), Sahih Muslim no. (2819), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (412), Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/219), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1419)].

Imam Ahmad said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Abu Sakhr informed me, from Ibn Qusayt, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he prayed, would stand until his two feet cracked [[In A: "until his feet split."]]."

Aishah said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, do you do this when Allah has forgiven you your previous sin and what will follow?" He said: "O Aishah, shall I not be a grateful servant?"

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih through the narration of Abd Allah ibn Wahb, with this chain [Al-Musnad (6/115), Sahih Muslim no. (2820)].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Awn al-Kharraz narrated to us, and he was trustworthy in Makkah, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us [[In A: "Bashir."]], Mis'ar narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood (in prayer) until his feet swelled, or he said his shins [swelled]. It was said to him: 'Has not Allah forgiven you your previous sin and what will follow?' He said: 'Shall I not be a grateful servant?'" This is a strange (gharib) narration from this route [Abu Ya'la narrated it in his Musnad (5/280) through the route of Abd Allah ibn Awn al-Kharraz with this chain. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad no. (2380), Kashf al-Astar, through the route of al-Husayn ibn al-Aswad from Muhammad ibn Bishr with this chain, and al-Bazzar said: "We do not know anyone who narrated this hadith with this chain except al-Husayn ibn Bishr and Abd Allah ibn Awn al-Kharraz. Others have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Bishr, from Mis'ar, from Ziyad ibn Ilaqah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, and this is the correct one." So al-Bazzar's statement here clarifies the words of al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir: "This is a strange narration from this route."]].

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory﴾, meaning: manifest and evident. What is meant by it is the Truce of al-Hudaybiyyah, for through it there came about abundant good. People became secure, some of them mixed with others, a believer spoke with a disbeliever, and beneficial knowledge and faith spread.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that Allah may forgive you your previous sin and what will follow﴾: this is one of his special qualities (khasa'is), peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in which no one else shares. And it is not established for anyone else, in terms of the reward of deeds, that his previous and later sins are forgiven. This is a great honor for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in all his affairs was upon obedience, righteousness and steadfastness, which no human other than him has attained, neither among the earlier nor the later generations. He is the most perfect of humanity without qualification, and their master in this world and the Hereafter. Since he was the most obedient of Allah's creation to Allah, and the most mindful of honoring His commands and prohibitions, when the she-camel knelt with him, he said: "The one who stopped the elephant has stopped her" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (2731, 2732).]]. Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me today for anything by which they honor the sanctities of Allah except that I will grant them it." So when he obeyed Allah in that and agreed to the truce, Allah said to him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your previous sin and what will follow, and complete His favor upon you﴾, meaning: in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾, meaning: by what He prescribes for you of the great Law and the upright religion.

﴿And Allah will help you with a mighty help﴾, meaning: because of your submission to the command of Allah, Allah will elevate you and help you against your enemies, as came in the authentic hadith: "Allah does not increase a servant through pardon except in honor, and no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him" [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2588) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. And from Umar ibn al-Khattab [(may Allah be pleased with him)] [[Addition from T.]], that he said: "You will not punish anyone who disobeys Allah, the Exalted, concerning you [in this world and the Hereafter] with the like of obeying Allah concerning him."

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿He is the One who sent down tranquility (al-sakinah)﴾, meaning: He placed serenity (al-tuma'ninah) (in their hearts). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, and it is also reported from him that it means mercy (al-rahmah).

Qatadah said: it is dignity (al-waqar) in the hearts of the believers. They were the Companions on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, who responded to Allah and His Messenger and submitted to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger. So when their hearts were at rest with that and settled, He increased them in faith along with their faith.

Al-Bukhari and other imams have used this verse as evidence that faith varies in strength within hearts.

Then Allah, the Exalted, mentioned that had He willed, He would have given victory over the disbelievers. So He said: ﴿And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: had He sent against them even a single angel, he would have annihilated their green (land and people). But Allah, the Exalted, prescribed for His believing servants jihad and fighting, because of the far-reaching wisdom, the conclusive proof, and the decisive evidence that He possesses in this. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is ever All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally﴾. The hadith of Anas has already been mentioned: they said, "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah; that is yours, so what is ours?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein eternally﴾, meaning: remaining therein forever. ﴿And remove from them their misdeeds﴾, meaning: their sins and wrongdoings, so that He does not punish them for them, but pardons, overlooks, forgives, covers over, shows mercy, and gives thanks. ﴿And that is with Allah a great achievement﴾, like His saying: ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has succeeded. And what is the worldly life except the enjoyment of delusion?﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 185].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women who assume about Allah an assumption of evil﴾, meaning: they accuse Allah regarding His judgment, and they presume about the Messenger and his Companions that they would be killed and wiped out entirely. For this reason He said: ﴿Upon them is the cycle of evil, and Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them﴾, meaning: He has removed them far from His mercy. ﴿And He has prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾.

Then He said, affirming His power to take vengeance upon the enemies—the enemies of Islam among the disbelievers and hypocrites: ﴿And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise﴾.
