Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness﴾, meaning over the creation, ﴿and a bringer of good news﴾, meaning to the believers, ﴿and a warner﴾, meaning to the disbelievers. Its explanation has already passed in Surah al-Ahzab, at the forty-fifth verse.

﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger and support him﴾. Ibn Abbas and others said: "and honour him," ﴿and respect him﴾, from tawqir, which means respect, reverence and magnification, ﴿and glorify Him﴾, meaning they glorify Allah, ﴿morning and evening﴾, meaning at the beginning of the day and its end.

Then Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger (ﷺ), honouring him, exalting him and esteeming him: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah﴾, like His saying: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 80]. ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾, meaning He is present with them, hearing their words, seeing their place, and knowing their inner thoughts and outward conduct. So Allah Himself is the one who receives the pledge through His Messenger (ﷺ), like His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who fulfils his covenant more than Allah? So rejoice in the transaction you have made. That is the great triumph﴾ [At-Tawbah: 111].

Ibn Abi Hatim has narrated: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, al-Fadl ibn Yahya al-Anbari told us, Ali ibn Bakkar told us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever draws his sword in the way of Allah, has pledged allegiance to Allah." [Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, as in al-Jami al-Saghir, and al-Suyuti graded it weak.]

My father told us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah told us, Jarir informed us, from Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khutham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at the Black Stone: "By Allah, Allah will raise it on the Day of Resurrection, having two eyes with which it sees, and a tongue with which it speaks, and it will testify for whoever touched it with truth. Whoever touches it has pledged allegiance to Allah." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah; the hand of Allah is over their hands﴾. [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 961, through Qutaybah from Jarir with its chain up to his words "testify for whoever touched it with truth," without mentioning the verse. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."]

Therefore He says here: ﴿So whoever breaks his oath only breaks it to his own detriment, and whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah – He will give him a great reward﴾, meaning the consequence of that breaking returns upon the one who breaks it, and Allah is not in need of him. ﴿Whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah – He will give him a great reward﴾, meaning abundant reward.

This pledge is the Pledge of Ridwan, which took place under a samur tree at al-Hudaybiyah. It is said that the Companions who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day numbered one thousand three hundred. It is said: four hundred. It is said: and five hundred. The middle figure is the most sound.

Mention of the narrations related to this:
Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah told us, Sufyan told us, from Amr, from Jabir, who said: On the day of al-Hudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred.

Muslim narrated it too from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same. Both of them also narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir, who said: We were on that day one thousand four hundred, and he placed his hand in that water, and water gushed from between his fingers until they all were satisfied. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4154 and Sahih Muslim no. 1856.]

This is an abridgement of another account, when he mentioned the story of their thirst on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them an arrow from his quiver, which they placed in the well of al-Hudaybiyah, and it gushed with water until it sufficed them. Jabir was asked: How many were you that day? He said: We were one thousand four hundred, and even if we had been one hundred thousand it would have sufficed us. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 5639.] In another narration in the Two Sahihs from Jabir, they were fifteen hundred. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4152 and Sahih Muslim no. 1856.]

Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Qatadah: I asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: How many were those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan? He said: fifteen hundred.
I said: But Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said they were fourteen hundred. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: He erred; he told me that they were fifteen hundred. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4153.]

Al-Bayhaqi said: This narration indicates that he used to say fifteen hundred in the past, then he mentioned the error and said fourteen hundred.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas that they were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five. The well-known report, related by many from him, is fourteen hundred, and this is what al-Bayhaqi narrated, from al-Hakim, from al-Asamm, from al-Abbas al-Duri, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, from Shababah ibn Sawwar, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from his father, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under the tree, one thousand four hundred. It is likewise in the narrations of Salamah ibn al-Akwa', Ma'qil ibn Yasar, and al-Bara' ibn Azib. Many scholars of the campaigns and biographies also hold this view. The two Sahihs have narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa say: The companions of the tree were one thousand four hundred, and the Aslam tribe that day were one-eighth of the Emigrants. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4155 and Sahih Muslim no. 1857.]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated in the Sirah, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, that they both told him: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, intending to visit the House, not intending fighting, and he drove with him seventy camels for sacrifice, and the people were seven hundred men, each camel for ten persons. Jabir ibn Abdullah, as it reached me from him, used to say: We, the companions of al-Hudaybiyah, were fourteen hundred. [See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham, 2/308.]

Thus said Ibn Ishaq, and this is counted among his errors, for the preserved report in the Two Sahihs is that they were a few hundred over a thousand (bid'a ashara mi'a).

Mention of the cause of this great pledge:
Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in the Sirah: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Makkah to convey on his behalf to the nobles of Quraysh what he had come for. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I fear Quraysh for myself, for there is no one from the Banu Adi ibn Ka'b in Makkah who would protect me, and Quraysh know my enmity towards them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honoured there than I am: Uthman ibn Affan. So he sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh, to inform them that he had not come for war, and that he had come as a visitor to this House and to honour its sanctity.

Uthman set out for Makkah, and Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-As met him when he entered Makkah, or before he entered it, and carried him in front of him, then gave him protection until he conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Uthman went until he came to Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Quraysh, and conveyed to them what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent him with. When Uthman finished delivering the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to them, they said to him: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate. He said: I will not do that until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulates it. Quraysh detained him with them, and word reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims that Uthman had been killed.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when word reached him that Uthman had been killed, said: "We will not leave until we fight these people." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people to the pledge. So the Pledge of Ridwan took place under the tree. The people used to say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged them to death. Jabir ibn Abdullah used to say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not pledge them to death, but he pledged us not to flee.

The people pledged allegiance, and none of the Muslims who attended it stayed behind except al-Jadd ibn Qays, of the Banu Salamah. Jabir used to say: By Allah, it is as if I am looking at him pressed against the armpit of his camel, cowering behind it to hide himself from the people. Then news came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that what had been said about Uthman was false.

Ibn Lahi'ah narrated from al-Aswad [in some copies: Abu al-Aswad], from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, a narration close to this context, and he added to it: that Quraysh sent, with Uthman [ibn Affan], Suhayl ibn Amr, Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza, and Mikraz ibn Hafs to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). While they were with them, an altercation occurred between some of the Muslims and some of the polytheists, and they threw arrows and stones at each other, and both groups shouted. Each group held the envoys who were with them. The herald of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: "Behold, the Holy Spirit has descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he has commanded the pledge; so go forth in the name of Allah and pledge allegiance." The Muslims went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was under the tree, and they pledged to him that they would never flee. This terrified the polytheists, and they released those of the Muslims who were with them, and called for a truce and peace.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdan informed us, Ahmad ibn Ubayd al-Saffar informed us, Tammam told us, al-Hasan ibn Bishr told us, al-Hakam ibn Abd al-Malik told us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded the Pledge of Ridwan, Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) was the envoy of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of Makkah. The people pledged allegiance, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, Uthman is in the need of Allah and the need of His Messenger." Then he struck one of his hands upon the other, and the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for Uthman was better than their hands for themselves. [I did not find it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, and perhaps it is in another work.]

Ibn Hisham said: Someone I trust told me, from one who narrated to him with a chain of his own, from Abu Mulaykah, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged allegiance on behalf of Uthman, striking one of his hands upon the other.

Abd al-Malik ibn Hisham al-Nahwi said: Waki' mentioned, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha'bi, that the first to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Pledge of Ridwan was Abu Sinan al-Asadi. [al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, 2/316.]

Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi said: Sufyan told us, Ibn Abi Khalid told us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people to the pledge, the first to reach him was Abu Sinan [al-Asadi, may Allah be pleased with him], and he said: "Extend your hand, and I will pledge to you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On what are you pledging to me?" Abu Sinan said: "On what is in your heart." This is Abu Sinan ibn Wahb al-Asadi [may Allah be pleased with him]. [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (4/137) through al-Humaydi.]

Ibn Kathir said: Al-Bukhari said: Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, having heard from al-Nadr ibn Muhammad: Sakhr [ibn al-Rabi'] narrated to us, from Nafi', who said: "People say that Ibn Umar embraced Islam before Umar, but that is not so. Rather, on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, Umar sent Abdullah to fetch his horse, which was with a man of the Ansar, so that he could fight on it, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking the pledge under the tree, and Umar did not know of it. Abdullah pledged allegiance, then went to the horse, brought it to Umar, and Umar was putting on his armour for battle. So he informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking the pledge under the tree. Umar set off and went with him until he pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It is this incident that people speak of when they say that Ibn Umar embraced Islam before Umar."

Then al-Bukhari said: Hisham ibn Ammar said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Umar ibn Muhammad al-'Umari narrated to us, Nafi' informed me, from Ibn Umar, that the people were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, having dispersed in the shade of the trees. Then suddenly the people were gathered around the Prophet ﷺ. He said, meaning Umar: "O Abdullah, look into what the people are doing, having gathered around the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He found them pledging allegiance, so he pledged allegiance, then returned to Umar, who went out and pledged allegiance.

Al-Bayhaqi traced this through Abu 'Amr al-Adib, from Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili, from al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, from Duhaym: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to me, and he mentioned it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4187).]

Al-Layth said, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah we were one thousand four hundred, and we pledged allegiance to him while Umar held his hand under the tree, which was a samurah tree. He said: We pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him for death." Muslim narrated it from Qutaybah, from him. [Sahih Muslim, no. (1856).]

Muslim also narrated from Yahya ibn Yahya, from Yazid ibn Zuray', from Khalid, from al-Hakam ibn Abdullah ibn al-A'raj, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: "I saw myself on the day of the tree while the Prophet ﷺ was taking the pledge from the people, and I was raising a branch of its branches away from his head, and we were fourteen hundred." He said: "We did not pledge allegiance to him for death, but we pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee." [Sahih Muslim, no. (1858).]

Al-Bukhari said: al-Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who said: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree." Yazid said: "I said: O Abu Muslim (in Muslim: Maslamah), upon what were you pledging allegiance that day?" He said: "Upon death." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2960).]

Al-Bukhari also said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd narrated to us, from Salamah, who said: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, then I withdrew, and he said: 'O Salamah, will you not pledge allegiance?' I said: 'I have pledged.' He said: 'Come forward and pledge.' So I drew near and pledged to him. I said: 'Upon what did you pledge him, O Salamah?' He said: 'Upon death.'" Muslim also narrated it by another route from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd. [Sahih Muslim, no. (1860).] Likewise al-Bukhari narrated from 'Abbad ibn Tamim that they pledged allegiance to him upon death. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2959).]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Fadl ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ahmad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr, narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar al-Yamami narrated to us, from Iyas ibn Salamah, from his father Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who said: "We came to al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we were fourteen hundred, and upon it were fifty sheep which did not quench our thirst. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on the edge of its well, meaning the well, and either he supplicated or he spat into it, and it bubbled up, and we drank and watered our animals." He said: "Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for the pledge at the foot of the tree. I was the first of the people to pledge to him, then he pledged and [others] pledged, until when he was in the middle of the people he said: 'Pledge to me, O Salamah.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have already pledged to you at the beginning of the people.' He said: 'And again.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me unarmed, so he gave me a shield, or a buckler. Then he pledged until, when he was at the end of the people, he said: 'Will you not pledge, O Salamah?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have pledged to you at the beginning and the middle of the people.' He said: 'And again.' So I pledged to him a third time. He said: 'O Salamah, where is your shield or buckler which I gave you?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, 'Amir met me unarmed, so I gave it to him.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, then said: 'You are like the one who said at first: O Allah, give me a beloved who is dearer to me than myself.'" He said: "Then the polytheists of Makkah sought a peace agreement with us, until some of us walked among others, and we made peace. I was a servant of Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah, may Allah be pleased with him, watering his horse, grooming it, and eating of his food, and I left my family and my property, emigrating to Allah and His Messenger. When we and the people of Makkah made peace, and we mingled with one another, I came to a tree, cleared away its thorns, then lay down in its shade at its base. Four of the polytheists of the people of Makkah came to me and began to revile the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I hated them. I moved to another tree, and they hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were thus, a caller called out from the bottom of the valley: 'O Muhajirun, Ibn Zunaym has been killed!' I drew my sword and charged at those four while they were sleeping, took their weapons, and made them a bundle in my hand. Then I said: 'By He who honoured the face of Muhammad ﷺ, none of you shall raise his head except that I strike the one in whom are his two eyes.'" He said: "Then I brought them, driving them before me, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. My uncle 'Amir came with a man from the 'Abalat called Mikraz, one of the polytheists, leading him, until we stood with them before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with seventy of the polytheists. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at them and said: 'Leave them; let them be the beginning of the wrongdoing and its continuation.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pardoned them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Makkah after He had given you victory over them﴾ [al-Fath: 24], to the end of the verse." [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah by al-Bayhaqi (4/138), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1807).]

Muslim narrated it in the same manner, or close to it, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Rahawayh with its chain.

It is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah, from Tariq, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "My father was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree. He said: We set out the following year as pilgrims, and the place of it was hidden from us. So if it became clear to you, then you know better." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4164), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1859), the wording being Muslim's.]

Abu Bakr al-Humaydi said: Sufyan narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the people to the pledge, we found a man among us called 'al-Jadd ibn Qays' hiding under the armpit of his camel."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn al-Zubayr, with it. [Musnad al-Humaydi (2/537), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1856).]

Al-Humaydi also said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, who heard Jabir say: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah we were one thousand four hundred, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: 'You are the best people on earth today.' Jabir said: 'If I could see, I would show you the place of the tree.' Sufyan said: 'They disagreed about its location.'" Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan. [Musnad al-Humaydi (2/514), Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4154), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1856).]

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "None who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire." [Al-Musnad (3/350).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas al-Makhrami narrated to us, Sa'd ibn 'Amr al-Ash'thi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi narrated to us, from Khidash ibn 'Ayyash, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "All who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter Paradise, except the owner of the red camel." He said: "So we set off racing to him, and behold, a man had lost his camel. We said: 'Come and pledge.' He said: 'Finding my camel is dearer to me than pledging.'" [In its chain is Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi, whom Ibn Ma'in weakened, and his shaykh Khidash ibn 'Ayyash, whom Ibn Hibban deemed trustworthy; al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know who this Khidash is."]

Abdullah ibn Ahmad said: Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Qurrah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Whoever ascends the Thaniyyah, the Thaniyyat al-Murar, will have forgiven him what was forgiven the Children of Israel." The first to ascend was the horsemen of the Banu al-Khazraj. Then the people hastened after them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every one of you is forgiven except the owner of the red camel." We said: "Come, that the Messenger of Allah [ﷺ] may ask forgiveness for you." He said: "By Allah, finding my lost animal is dearer to me than that your companion ask forgiveness for me." Then behold, he was a man searching for his lost animal. Muslim narrated it from Ubaydullah, with it. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2780).]

Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir say: Umm Mubashshir informed me that she heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say at the house of Hafsah: "None of the Companions of the Tree who pledged allegiance under it will enter the Fire, God willing." She said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He rebuked her, and she said to Hafsah: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ [Maryam: 71]. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has said: ﴿Then We will save those who feared Allah, and We will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾ [Maryam: 72]." Muslim narrated it. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2496).]

Also in it, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: that a slave of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah came complaining about Hatib, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Hatib will surely enter the Fire." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You lie; he will not enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2494).]

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said in praise of them: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you pledge allegiance only to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So he who breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself, and he who fulfils that which he has promised Allah – He will give him a great reward﴾ [al-Fath: 10], as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree; so He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with an imminent victory﴾ [al-Fath: 18].

Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness﴾, meaning over the creation, ﴿and a bringer of good news﴾, meaning to the believers, ﴿and a warner﴾, meaning to the disbelievers. Its explanation has already passed in Surah al-Ahzab, at the forty-fifth verse.

﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger and support him﴾. Ibn Abbas and others said: "and honour him," ﴿and respect him﴾, from tawqir, which means respect, reverence and magnification, ﴿and glorify Him﴾, meaning they glorify Allah, ﴿morning and evening﴾, meaning at the beginning of the day and its end.

Then Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger (ﷺ), honouring him, exalting him and esteeming him: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah﴾, like His saying: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 80]. ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾, meaning He is present with them, hearing their words, seeing their place, and knowing their inner thoughts and outward conduct. So Allah Himself is the one who receives the pledge through His Messenger (ﷺ), like His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who fulfils his covenant more than Allah? So rejoice in the transaction you have made. That is the great triumph﴾ [At-Tawbah: 111].

Ibn Abi Hatim has narrated: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, al-Fadl ibn Yahya al-Anbari told us, Ali ibn Bakkar told us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever draws his sword in the way of Allah, has pledged allegiance to Allah." [Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, as in al-Jami al-Saghir, and al-Suyuti graded it weak.]

My father told us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah told us, Jarir informed us, from Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khutham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at the Black Stone: "By Allah, Allah will raise it on the Day of Resurrection, having two eyes with which it sees, and a tongue with which it speaks, and it will testify for whoever touched it with truth. Whoever touches it has pledged allegiance to Allah." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah; the hand of Allah is over their hands﴾. [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 961, through Qutaybah from Jarir with its chain up to his words "testify for whoever touched it with truth," without mentioning the verse. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."]

Therefore He says here: ﴿So whoever breaks his oath only breaks it to his own detriment, and whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah – He will give him a great reward﴾, meaning the consequence of that breaking returns upon the one who breaks it, and Allah is not in need of him. ﴿Whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah – He will give him a great reward﴾, meaning abundant reward.

This pledge is the Pledge of Ridwan, which took place under a samur tree at al-Hudaybiyah. It is said that the Companions who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day numbered one thousand three hundred. It is said: four hundred. It is said: and five hundred. The middle figure is the most sound.

Mention of the narrations related to this:
Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah told us, Sufyan told us, from Amr, from Jabir, who said: On the day of al-Hudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred.

Muslim narrated it too from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same. Both of them also narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir, who said: We were on that day one thousand four hundred, and he placed his hand in that water, and water gushed from between his fingers until they all were satisfied. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4154 and Sahih Muslim no. 1856.]

This is an abridgement of another account, when he mentioned the story of their thirst on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them an arrow from his quiver, which they placed in the well of al-Hudaybiyah, and it gushed with water until it sufficed them. Jabir was asked: How many were you that day? He said: We were one thousand four hundred, and even if we had been one hundred thousand it would have sufficed us. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 5639.] In another narration in the Two Sahihs from Jabir, they were fifteen hundred. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4152 and Sahih Muslim no. 1856.]

Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Qatadah: I asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: How many were those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan? He said: fifteen hundred.
I said: But Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said they were fourteen hundred. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: He erred; he told me that they were fifteen hundred. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4153.]

Al-Bayhaqi said: This narration indicates that he used to say fifteen hundred in the past, then he mentioned the error and said fourteen hundred.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas that they were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five. The well-known report, related by many from him, is fourteen hundred, and this is what al-Bayhaqi narrated, from al-Hakim, from al-Asamm, from al-Abbas al-Duri, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, from Shababah ibn Sawwar, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from his father, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under the tree, one thousand four hundred. It is likewise in the narrations of Salamah ibn al-Akwa', Ma'qil ibn Yasar, and al-Bara' ibn Azib. Many scholars of the campaigns and biographies also hold this view. The two Sahihs have narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa say: The companions of the tree were one thousand four hundred, and the Aslam tribe that day were one-eighth of the Emigrants. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4155 and Sahih Muslim no. 1857.]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated in the Sirah, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, that they both told him: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, intending to visit the House, not intending fighting, and he drove with him seventy camels for sacrifice, and the people were seven hundred men, each camel for ten persons. Jabir ibn Abdullah, as it reached me from him, used to say: We, the companions of al-Hudaybiyah, were fourteen hundred. [See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham, 2/308.]

Thus said Ibn Ishaq, and this is counted among his errors, for the preserved report in the Two Sahihs is that they were a few hundred over a thousand (bid'a ashara mi'a).

Mention of the cause of this great pledge:
Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in the Sirah: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Makkah to convey on his behalf to the nobles of Quraysh what he had come for. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I fear Quraysh for myself, for there is no one from the Banu Adi ibn Ka'b in Makkah who would protect me, and Quraysh know my enmity towards them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honoured there than I am: Uthman ibn Affan. So he sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh, to inform them that he had not come for war, and that he had come as a visitor to this House and to honour its sanctity.

Uthman set out for Makkah, and Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-As met him when he entered Makkah, or before he entered it, and carried him in front of him, then gave him protection until he conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Uthman went until he came to Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Quraysh, and conveyed to them what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent him with. When Uthman finished delivering the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to them, they said to him: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate. He said: I will not do that until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulates it. Quraysh detained him with them, and word reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims that Uthman had been killed.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when word reached him that Uthman had been killed, said: "We will not leave until we fight these people." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people to the pledge. So the Pledge of Ridwan took place under the tree. The people used to say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged them to death. Jabir ibn Abdullah used to say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not pledge them to death, but he pledged us not to flee.

The people pledged allegiance, and none of the Muslims who attended it stayed behind except al-Jadd ibn Qays, of the Banu Salamah. Jabir used to say: By Allah, it is as if I am looking at him pressed against the armpit of his camel, cowering behind it to hide himself from the people. Then news came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that what had been said about Uthman was false.

Ibn Lahi'ah narrated from al-Aswad [in some copies: Abu al-Aswad], from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, a narration close to this context, and he added to it: that Quraysh sent, with Uthman [ibn Affan], Suhayl ibn Amr, Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza, and Mikraz ibn Hafs to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). While they were with them, an altercation occurred between some of the Muslims and some of the polytheists, and they threw arrows and stones at each other, and both groups shouted. Each group held the envoys who were with them. The herald of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: "Behold, the Holy Spirit has descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he has commanded the pledge; so go forth in the name of Allah and pledge allegiance." The Muslims went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was under the tree, and they pledged to him that they would never flee. This terrified the polytheists, and they released those of the Muslims who were with them, and called for a truce and peace.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdan informed us, Ahmad ibn Ubayd al-Saffar informed us, Tammam told us, al-Hasan ibn Bishr told us, al-Hakam ibn Abd al-Malik told us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded the Pledge of Ridwan, Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) was the envoy of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of Makkah. The people pledged allegiance, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, Uthman is in the need of Allah and the need of His Messenger." Then he struck one of his hands upon the other, and the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for Uthman was better than their hands for themselves. [I did not find it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, and perhaps it is in another work.]

Ibn Hisham said: Someone I trust told me, from one who narrated to him with a chain of his own, from Abu Mulaykah, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged allegiance on behalf of Uthman, striking one of his hands upon the other.

Abd al-Malik ibn Hisham al-Nahwi said: Waki' mentioned, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha'bi, that the first to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Pledge of Ridwan was Abu Sinan al-Asadi. [al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, 2/316.]

Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi said: Sufyan told us, Ibn Abi Khalid told us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people to the pledge, the first to reach him was Abu Sinan [al-Asadi, may Allah be pleased with him], and he said: "Extend your hand, and I will pledge to you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On what are you pledging to me?" Abu Sinan said: "On what is in your heart." This is Abu Sinan ibn Wahb al-Asadi [may Allah be pleased with him]. [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (4/137) through al-Humaydi.]

Ibn Kathir said: Al-Bukhari said: Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, having heard from al-Nadr ibn Muhammad: Sakhr [ibn al-Rabi'] narrated to us, from Nafi', who said: "People say that Ibn Umar embraced Islam before Umar, but that is not so. Rather, on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, Umar sent Abdullah to fetch his horse, which was with a man of the Ansar, so that he could fight on it, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking the pledge under the tree, and Umar did not know of it. Abdullah pledged allegiance, then went to the horse, brought it to Umar, and Umar was putting on his armour for battle. So he informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking the pledge under the tree. Umar set off and went with him until he pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It is this incident that people speak of when they say that Ibn Umar embraced Islam before Umar."

Then al-Bukhari said: Hisham ibn Ammar said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Umar ibn Muhammad al-'Umari narrated to us, Nafi' informed me, from Ibn Umar, that the people were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, having dispersed in the shade of the trees. Then suddenly the people were gathered around the Prophet ﷺ. He said, meaning Umar: "O Abdullah, look into what the people are doing, having gathered around the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He found them pledging allegiance, so he pledged allegiance, then returned to Umar, who went out and pledged allegiance.

Al-Bayhaqi traced this through Abu 'Amr al-Adib, from Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili, from al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, from Duhaym: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to me, and he mentioned it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4187).]

Al-Layth said, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah we were one thousand four hundred, and we pledged allegiance to him while Umar held his hand under the tree, which was a samurah tree. He said: We pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him for death." Muslim narrated it from Qutaybah, from him. [Sahih Muslim, no. (1856).]

Muslim also narrated from Yahya ibn Yahya, from Yazid ibn Zuray', from Khalid, from al-Hakam ibn Abdullah ibn al-A'raj, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: "I saw myself on the day of the tree while the Prophet ﷺ was taking the pledge from the people, and I was raising a branch of its branches away from his head, and we were fourteen hundred." He said: "We did not pledge allegiance to him for death, but we pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee." [Sahih Muslim, no. (1858).]

Al-Bukhari said: al-Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who said: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree." Yazid said: "I said: O Abu Muslim (in Muslim: Maslamah), upon what were you pledging allegiance that day?" He said: "Upon death." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2960).]

Al-Bukhari also said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd narrated to us, from Salamah, who said: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, then I withdrew, and he said: 'O Salamah, will you not pledge allegiance?' I said: 'I have pledged.' He said: 'Come forward and pledge.' So I drew near and pledged to him. I said: 'Upon what did you pledge him, O Salamah?' He said: 'Upon death.'" Muslim also narrated it by another route from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd. [Sahih Muslim, no. (1860).] Likewise al-Bukhari narrated from 'Abbad ibn Tamim that they pledged allegiance to him upon death. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2959).]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Fadl ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ahmad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr, narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar al-Yamami narrated to us, from Iyas ibn Salamah, from his father Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who said: "We came to al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we were fourteen hundred, and upon it were fifty sheep which did not quench our thirst. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on the edge of its well, meaning the well, and either he supplicated or he spat into it, and it bubbled up, and we drank and watered our animals." He said: "Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for the pledge at the foot of the tree. I was the first of the people to pledge to him, then he pledged and [others] pledged, until when he was in the middle of the people he said: 'Pledge to me, O Salamah.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have already pledged to you at the beginning of the people.' He said: 'And again.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me unarmed, so he gave me a shield, or a buckler. Then he pledged until, when he was at the end of the people, he said: 'Will you not pledge, O Salamah?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have pledged to you at the beginning and the middle of the people.' He said: 'And again.' So I pledged to him a third time. He said: 'O Salamah, where is your shield or buckler which I gave you?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, 'Amir met me unarmed, so I gave it to him.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, then said: 'You are like the one who said at first: O Allah, give me a beloved who is dearer to me than myself.'" He said: "Then the polytheists of Makkah sought a peace agreement with us, until some of us walked among others, and we made peace. I was a servant of Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah, may Allah be pleased with him, watering his horse, grooming it, and eating of his food, and I left my family and my property, emigrating to Allah and His Messenger. When we and the people of Makkah made peace, and we mingled with one another, I came to a tree, cleared away its thorns, then lay down in its shade at its base. Four of the polytheists of the people of Makkah came to me and began to revile the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I hated them. I moved to another tree, and they hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were thus, a caller called out from the bottom of the valley: 'O Muhajirun, Ibn Zunaym has been killed!' I drew my sword and charged at those four while they were sleeping, took their weapons, and made them a bundle in my hand. Then I said: 'By He who honoured the face of Muhammad ﷺ, none of you shall raise his head except that I strike the one in whom are his two eyes.'" He said: "Then I brought them, driving them before me, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. My uncle 'Amir came with a man from the 'Abalat called Mikraz, one of the polytheists, leading him, until we stood with them before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with seventy of the polytheists. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at them and said: 'Leave them; let them be the beginning of the wrongdoing and its continuation.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pardoned them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Makkah after He had given you victory over them﴾ [al-Fath: 24], to the end of the verse." [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah by al-Bayhaqi (4/138), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1807).]

Muslim narrated it in the same manner, or close to it, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Rahawayh with its chain.

It is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah, from Tariq, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "My father was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree. He said: We set out the following year as pilgrims, and the place of it was hidden from us. So if it became clear to you, then you know better." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4164), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1859), the wording being Muslim's.]

Abu Bakr al-Humaydi said: Sufyan narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the people to the pledge, we found a man among us called 'al-Jadd ibn Qays' hiding under the armpit of his camel."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn al-Zubayr, with it. [Musnad al-Humaydi (2/537), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1856).]

Al-Humaydi also said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, who heard Jabir say: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah we were one thousand four hundred, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: 'You are the best people on earth today.' Jabir said: 'If I could see, I would show you the place of the tree.' Sufyan said: 'They disagreed about its location.'" Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan. [Musnad al-Humaydi (2/514), Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4154), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1856).]

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "None who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire." [Al-Musnad (3/350).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas al-Makhrami narrated to us, Sa'd ibn 'Amr al-Ash'thi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi narrated to us, from Khidash ibn 'Ayyash, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "All who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter Paradise, except the owner of the red camel." He said: "So we set off racing to him, and behold, a man had lost his camel. We said: 'Come and pledge.' He said: 'Finding my camel is dearer to me than pledging.'" [In its chain is Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi, whom Ibn Ma'in weakened, and his shaykh Khidash ibn 'Ayyash, whom Ibn Hibban deemed trustworthy; al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know who this Khidash is."]

Abdullah ibn Ahmad said: Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Qurrah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Whoever ascends the Thaniyyah, the Thaniyyat al-Murar, will have forgiven him what was forgiven the Children of Israel." The first to ascend was the horsemen of the Banu al-Khazraj. Then the people hastened after them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every one of you is forgiven except the owner of the red camel." We said: "Come, that the Messenger of Allah [ﷺ] may ask forgiveness for you." He said: "By Allah, finding my lost animal is dearer to me than that your companion ask forgiveness for me." Then behold, he was a man searching for his lost animal. Muslim narrated it from Ubaydullah, with it. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2780).]

Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir say: Umm Mubashshir informed me that she heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say at the house of Hafsah: "None of the Companions of the Tree who pledged allegiance under it will enter the Fire, God willing." She said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He rebuked her, and she said to Hafsah: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ [Maryam: 71]. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has said: ﴿Then We will save those who feared Allah, and We will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾ [Maryam: 72]." Muslim narrated it. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2496).]

Also in it, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: that a slave of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah came complaining about Hatib, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Hatib will surely enter the Fire." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You lie; he will not enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2494).]

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said in praise of them: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you pledge allegiance only to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So he who breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself, and he who fulfils that which he has promised Allah – He will give him a great reward﴾ [al-Fath: 10], as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree; so He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with an imminent victory﴾ [al-Fath: 18].

Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness﴾, meaning over the creation, ﴿and a bringer of good news﴾, meaning to the believers, ﴿and a warner﴾, meaning to the disbelievers. Its explanation has already passed in Surah al-Ahzab, at the forty-fifth verse.

﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger and support him﴾. Ibn Abbas and others said: "and honour him," ﴿and respect him﴾, from tawqir, which means respect, reverence and magnification, ﴿and glorify Him﴾, meaning they glorify Allah, ﴿morning and evening﴾, meaning at the beginning of the day and its end.

Then Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger (ﷺ), honouring him, exalting him and esteeming him: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah﴾, like His saying: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 80]. ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands﴾, meaning He is present with them, hearing their words, seeing their place, and knowing their inner thoughts and outward conduct. So Allah Himself is the one who receives the pledge through His Messenger (ﷺ), like His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who fulfils his covenant more than Allah? So rejoice in the transaction you have made. That is the great triumph﴾ [At-Tawbah: 111].

Ibn Abi Hatim has narrated: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, al-Fadl ibn Yahya al-Anbari told us, Ali ibn Bakkar told us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever draws his sword in the way of Allah, has pledged allegiance to Allah." [Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, as in al-Jami al-Saghir, and al-Suyuti graded it weak.]

My father told us, Yahya ibn al-Mughirah told us, Jarir informed us, from Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khutham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at the Black Stone: "By Allah, Allah will raise it on the Day of Resurrection, having two eyes with which it sees, and a tongue with which it speaks, and it will testify for whoever touched it with truth. Whoever touches it has pledged allegiance to Allah." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah; the hand of Allah is over their hands﴾. [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 961, through Qutaybah from Jarir with its chain up to his words "testify for whoever touched it with truth," without mentioning the verse. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."]

Therefore He says here: ﴿So whoever breaks his oath only breaks it to his own detriment, and whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah – He will give him a great reward﴾, meaning the consequence of that breaking returns upon the one who breaks it, and Allah is not in need of him. ﴿Whoever fulfils what he has covenanted with Allah – He will give him a great reward﴾, meaning abundant reward.

This pledge is the Pledge of Ridwan, which took place under a samur tree at al-Hudaybiyah. It is said that the Companions who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day numbered one thousand three hundred. It is said: four hundred. It is said: and five hundred. The middle figure is the most sound.

Mention of the narrations related to this:
Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah told us, Sufyan told us, from Amr, from Jabir, who said: On the day of al-Hudaybiyah we were one thousand four hundred.

Muslim narrated it too from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with the same. Both of them also narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir, who said: We were on that day one thousand four hundred, and he placed his hand in that water, and water gushed from between his fingers until they all were satisfied. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4154 and Sahih Muslim no. 1856.]

This is an abridgement of another account, when he mentioned the story of their thirst on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them an arrow from his quiver, which they placed in the well of al-Hudaybiyah, and it gushed with water until it sufficed them. Jabir was asked: How many were you that day? He said: We were one thousand four hundred, and even if we had been one hundred thousand it would have sufficed us. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 5639.] In another narration in the Two Sahihs from Jabir, they were fifteen hundred. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4152 and Sahih Muslim no. 1856.]

Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Qatadah: I asked Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: How many were those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan? He said: fifteen hundred.
I said: But Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said they were fourteen hundred. He said, may Allah have mercy on him: He erred; he told me that they were fifteen hundred. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4153.]

Al-Bayhaqi said: This narration indicates that he used to say fifteen hundred in the past, then he mentioned the error and said fourteen hundred.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas that they were one thousand five hundred and twenty-five. The well-known report, related by many from him, is fourteen hundred, and this is what al-Bayhaqi narrated, from al-Hakim, from al-Asamm, from al-Abbas al-Duri, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, from Shababah ibn Sawwar, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from his father, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under the tree, one thousand four hundred. It is likewise in the narrations of Salamah ibn al-Akwa', Ma'qil ibn Yasar, and al-Bara' ibn Azib. Many scholars of the campaigns and biographies also hold this view. The two Sahihs have narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa say: The companions of the tree were one thousand four hundred, and the Aslam tribe that day were one-eighth of the Emigrants. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4155 and Sahih Muslim no. 1857.]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated in the Sirah, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, that they both told him: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, intending to visit the House, not intending fighting, and he drove with him seventy camels for sacrifice, and the people were seven hundred men, each camel for ten persons. Jabir ibn Abdullah, as it reached me from him, used to say: We, the companions of al-Hudaybiyah, were fourteen hundred. [See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham, 2/308.]

Thus said Ibn Ishaq, and this is counted among his errors, for the preserved report in the Two Sahihs is that they were a few hundred over a thousand (bid'a ashara mi'a).

Mention of the cause of this great pledge:
Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said in the Sirah: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Makkah to convey on his behalf to the nobles of Quraysh what he had come for. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I fear Quraysh for myself, for there is no one from the Banu Adi ibn Ka'b in Makkah who would protect me, and Quraysh know my enmity towards them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honoured there than I am: Uthman ibn Affan. So he sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of Quraysh, to inform them that he had not come for war, and that he had come as a visitor to this House and to honour its sanctity.

Uthman set out for Makkah, and Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-As met him when he entered Makkah, or before he entered it, and carried him in front of him, then gave him protection until he conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Uthman went until he came to Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Quraysh, and conveyed to them what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent him with. When Uthman finished delivering the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to them, they said to him: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate. He said: I will not do that until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulates it. Quraysh detained him with them, and word reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims that Uthman had been killed.

Ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when word reached him that Uthman had been killed, said: "We will not leave until we fight these people." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people to the pledge. So the Pledge of Ridwan took place under the tree. The people used to say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged them to death. Jabir ibn Abdullah used to say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not pledge them to death, but he pledged us not to flee.

The people pledged allegiance, and none of the Muslims who attended it stayed behind except al-Jadd ibn Qays, of the Banu Salamah. Jabir used to say: By Allah, it is as if I am looking at him pressed against the armpit of his camel, cowering behind it to hide himself from the people. Then news came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that what had been said about Uthman was false.

Ibn Lahi'ah narrated from al-Aswad [in some copies: Abu al-Aswad], from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, a narration close to this context, and he added to it: that Quraysh sent, with Uthman [ibn Affan], Suhayl ibn Amr, Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza, and Mikraz ibn Hafs to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). While they were with them, an altercation occurred between some of the Muslims and some of the polytheists, and they threw arrows and stones at each other, and both groups shouted. Each group held the envoys who were with them. The herald of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: "Behold, the Holy Spirit has descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he has commanded the pledge; so go forth in the name of Allah and pledge allegiance." The Muslims went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was under the tree, and they pledged to him that they would never flee. This terrified the polytheists, and they released those of the Muslims who were with them, and called for a truce and peace.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdan informed us, Ahmad ibn Ubayd al-Saffar informed us, Tammam told us, al-Hasan ibn Bishr told us, al-Hakam ibn Abd al-Malik told us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded the Pledge of Ridwan, Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) was the envoy of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of Makkah. The people pledged allegiance, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, Uthman is in the need of Allah and the need of His Messenger." Then he struck one of his hands upon the other, and the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for Uthman was better than their hands for themselves. [I did not find it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, and perhaps it is in another work.]

Ibn Hisham said: Someone I trust told me, from one who narrated to him with a chain of his own, from Abu Mulaykah, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pledged allegiance on behalf of Uthman, striking one of his hands upon the other.

Abd al-Malik ibn Hisham al-Nahwi said: Waki' mentioned, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha'bi, that the first to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Pledge of Ridwan was Abu Sinan al-Asadi. [al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, 2/316.]

Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi said: Sufyan told us, Ibn Abi Khalid told us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people to the pledge, the first to reach him was Abu Sinan [al-Asadi, may Allah be pleased with him], and he said: "Extend your hand, and I will pledge to you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On what are you pledging to me?" Abu Sinan said: "On what is in your heart." This is Abu Sinan ibn Wahb al-Asadi [may Allah be pleased with him]. [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (4/137) through al-Humaydi.]

Ibn Kathir said: Al-Bukhari said: Shuja' ibn al-Walid narrated to us, having heard from al-Nadr ibn Muhammad: Sakhr [ibn al-Rabi'] narrated to us, from Nafi', who said: "People say that Ibn Umar embraced Islam before Umar, but that is not so. Rather, on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, Umar sent Abdullah to fetch his horse, which was with a man of the Ansar, so that he could fight on it, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking the pledge under the tree, and Umar did not know of it. Abdullah pledged allegiance, then went to the horse, brought it to Umar, and Umar was putting on his armour for battle. So he informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taking the pledge under the tree. Umar set off and went with him until he pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It is this incident that people speak of when they say that Ibn Umar embraced Islam before Umar."

Then al-Bukhari said: Hisham ibn Ammar said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Umar ibn Muhammad al-'Umari narrated to us, Nafi' informed me, from Ibn Umar, that the people were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, having dispersed in the shade of the trees. Then suddenly the people were gathered around the Prophet ﷺ. He said, meaning Umar: "O Abdullah, look into what the people are doing, having gathered around the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He found them pledging allegiance, so he pledged allegiance, then returned to Umar, who went out and pledged allegiance.

Al-Bayhaqi traced this through Abu 'Amr al-Adib, from Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili, from al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, from Duhaym: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to me, and he mentioned it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4187).]

Al-Layth said, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah we were one thousand four hundred, and we pledged allegiance to him while Umar held his hand under the tree, which was a samurah tree. He said: We pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee, and we did not pledge allegiance to him for death." Muslim narrated it from Qutaybah, from him. [Sahih Muslim, no. (1856).]

Muslim also narrated from Yahya ibn Yahya, from Yazid ibn Zuray', from Khalid, from al-Hakam ibn Abdullah ibn al-A'raj, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: "I saw myself on the day of the tree while the Prophet ﷺ was taking the pledge from the people, and I was raising a branch of its branches away from his head, and we were fourteen hundred." He said: "We did not pledge allegiance to him for death, but we pledged allegiance to him that we would not flee." [Sahih Muslim, no. (1858).]

Al-Bukhari said: al-Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who said: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree." Yazid said: "I said: O Abu Muslim (in Muslim: Maslamah), upon what were you pledging allegiance that day?" He said: "Upon death." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2960).]

Al-Bukhari also said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd narrated to us, from Salamah, who said: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, then I withdrew, and he said: 'O Salamah, will you not pledge allegiance?' I said: 'I have pledged.' He said: 'Come forward and pledge.' So I drew near and pledged to him. I said: 'Upon what did you pledge him, O Salamah?' He said: 'Upon death.'" Muslim also narrated it by another route from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd. [Sahih Muslim, no. (1860).] Likewise al-Bukhari narrated from 'Abbad ibn Tamim that they pledged allegiance to him upon death. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2959).]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Fadl ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ahmad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr, narrated to us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar al-Yamami narrated to us, from Iyas ibn Salamah, from his father Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who said: "We came to al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we were fourteen hundred, and upon it were fifty sheep which did not quench our thirst. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on the edge of its well, meaning the well, and either he supplicated or he spat into it, and it bubbled up, and we drank and watered our animals." He said: "Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for the pledge at the foot of the tree. I was the first of the people to pledge to him, then he pledged and [others] pledged, until when he was in the middle of the people he said: 'Pledge to me, O Salamah.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have already pledged to you at the beginning of the people.' He said: 'And again.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me unarmed, so he gave me a shield, or a buckler. Then he pledged until, when he was at the end of the people, he said: 'Will you not pledge, O Salamah?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have pledged to you at the beginning and the middle of the people.' He said: 'And again.' So I pledged to him a third time. He said: 'O Salamah, where is your shield or buckler which I gave you?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, 'Amir met me unarmed, so I gave it to him.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, then said: 'You are like the one who said at first: O Allah, give me a beloved who is dearer to me than myself.'" He said: "Then the polytheists of Makkah sought a peace agreement with us, until some of us walked among others, and we made peace. I was a servant of Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah, may Allah be pleased with him, watering his horse, grooming it, and eating of his food, and I left my family and my property, emigrating to Allah and His Messenger. When we and the people of Makkah made peace, and we mingled with one another, I came to a tree, cleared away its thorns, then lay down in its shade at its base. Four of the polytheists of the people of Makkah came to me and began to revile the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I hated them. I moved to another tree, and they hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were thus, a caller called out from the bottom of the valley: 'O Muhajirun, Ibn Zunaym has been killed!' I drew my sword and charged at those four while they were sleeping, took their weapons, and made them a bundle in my hand. Then I said: 'By He who honoured the face of Muhammad ﷺ, none of you shall raise his head except that I strike the one in whom are his two eyes.'" He said: "Then I brought them, driving them before me, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. My uncle 'Amir came with a man from the 'Abalat called Mikraz, one of the polytheists, leading him, until we stood with them before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with seventy of the polytheists. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at them and said: 'Leave them; let them be the beginning of the wrongdoing and its continuation.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pardoned them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the heart of Makkah after He had given you victory over them﴾ [al-Fath: 24], to the end of the verse." [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah by al-Bayhaqi (4/138), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1807).]

Muslim narrated it in the same manner, or close to it, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Rahawayh with its chain.

It is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah, from Tariq, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "My father was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ under the tree. He said: We set out the following year as pilgrims, and the place of it was hidden from us. So if it became clear to you, then you know better." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4164), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1859), the wording being Muslim's.]

Abu Bakr al-Humaydi said: Sufyan narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called the people to the pledge, we found a man among us called 'al-Jadd ibn Qays' hiding under the armpit of his camel."

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn al-Zubayr, with it. [Musnad al-Humaydi (2/537), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1856).]

Al-Humaydi also said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, who heard Jabir say: "On the day of al-Hudaybiyyah we were one thousand four hundred, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: 'You are the best people on earth today.' Jabir said: 'If I could see, I would show you the place of the tree.' Sufyan said: 'They disagreed about its location.'" Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan. [Musnad al-Humaydi (2/514), Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4154), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1856).]

Imam Ahmad said: Yunus narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "None who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire." [Al-Musnad (3/350).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas al-Makhrami narrated to us, Sa'd ibn 'Amr al-Ash'thi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi narrated to us, from Khidash ibn 'Ayyash, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "All who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter Paradise, except the owner of the red camel." He said: "So we set off racing to him, and behold, a man had lost his camel. We said: 'Come and pledge.' He said: 'Finding my camel is dearer to me than pledging.'" [In its chain is Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Abdi, whom Ibn Ma'in weakened, and his shaykh Khidash ibn 'Ayyash, whom Ibn Hibban deemed trustworthy; al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know who this Khidash is."]

Abdullah ibn Ahmad said: Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Qurrah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Whoever ascends the Thaniyyah, the Thaniyyat al-Murar, will have forgiven him what was forgiven the Children of Israel." The first to ascend was the horsemen of the Banu al-Khazraj. Then the people hastened after them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every one of you is forgiven except the owner of the red camel." We said: "Come, that the Messenger of Allah [ﷺ] may ask forgiveness for you." He said: "By Allah, finding my lost animal is dearer to me than that your companion ask forgiveness for me." Then behold, he was a man searching for his lost animal. Muslim narrated it from Ubaydullah, with it. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2780).]

Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir say: Umm Mubashshir informed me that she heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say at the house of Hafsah: "None of the Companions of the Tree who pledged allegiance under it will enter the Fire, God willing." She said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He rebuked her, and she said to Hafsah: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾ [Maryam: 71]. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has said: ﴿Then We will save those who feared Allah, and We will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾ [Maryam: 72]." Muslim narrated it. [Sahih Muslim, no. (2496).]

Also in it, from Qutaybah, from al-Layth, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: that a slave of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah came complaining about Hatib, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Hatib will surely enter the Fire." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You lie; he will not enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2494).]

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said in praise of them: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you pledge allegiance only to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands. So he who breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself, and he who fulfils that which he has promised Allah – He will give him a great reward﴾ [al-Fath: 10], as Allah the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree; so He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down tranquillity upon them and rewarded them with an imminent victory﴾ [al-Fath: 18].

Allah, the Exalted, says, informing His Messenger (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) about what the desert Arabs who stayed behind would offer as excuses. They were those who preferred to remain with their families and their occupations, and abandoned marching with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So they made their preoccupation with these matters an excuse, and asked the Messenger ﷺ to seek forgiveness for them. This was a statement from them not made out of genuine belief, but out of dissimulation and flattery. Therefore Allah says: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say: "Who then can avail you anything against Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you benefit?"﴾ That is: no one can avert what He has decreed for you, exalted and sanctified is He, and He knows your secrets and your inner thoughts, even if you flatter us and follow us. Therefore He says: ﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do.﴾

Then He says: ﴿Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again.﴾ That is: your staying behind was not the staying behind of one who has an excuse, nor of one who is disobedient, but the staying behind of hypocrisy. ﴿Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again.﴾ That is: you believed that they would be killed, that their roots would be uprooted, that their green would be destroyed, and that none of them would return to bring news. ﴿And you harbored an evil assumption, and you were a people doomed.﴾ That is: lost (halkā). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and others. Qatadah said: corrupt. It was also said: the word is in the dialect of 'Uman.

Then He says: ﴿And whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ That is: whoever does not sincerely direct his deeds, outwardly and inwardly, to Allah, then Allah, the Exalted, will punish him in the Blaze, even if he displays to people what they believe, contrary to what he actually is in reality.

Then Allah, the Exalted, made clear that He is the Judge, the Owner, the Disposer of the affairs of the people of the heavens and the earth: ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ That is: to whoever repents to Him, turns to Him in submission, and humbles himself before Him.

The Exalted says, informing about the Bedouin Arabs who stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ at the expedition of al-Hudaybiyah [[In T, M, A: "'Umrah".]], when the Prophet ﷺ and his companions went to Khaybar to conquer it: they asked to go out with them to the spoils (maghanim), though they had held back from the time of fighting the enemy, struggling against them, and enduring them. So God commanded His Messenger ﷺ not to permit them in that, as a punishment for them of the same kind as their sin. God had promised the people of al-Hudaybiyah the spoils of Khaybar alone, with none of the stay-behind Bedouins sharing in them. Therefore nothing other than that occurs, by the Law (shar') and by Decree (qadar). For this reason He said: ﴿They want to change the words of God﴾.

Mujahid, Qatadah and Juwaybir said: it is the promise that was given to the people of al-Hudaybiyah. Ibn Jarir [Tafsir al-Tabari (26/50)] also chose this view.

Ibn Zayd said: it is His saying: ﴿So if God brings you back to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, then say: "You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me. You were pleased with sitting at home the first time, so sit with those who stay behind."﴾ [al-Tawbah: 83].

What Ibn Zayd said is open to question, because that verse in Bara'ah (al-Tawbah) was revealed concerning the expedition of Tabuk, and it came later than the expedition of al-Hudaybiyah [[In T, M, A: "'Umrah".]].

Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿They want to change the words of God﴾ means: by discouraging the Muslims from jihad.

﴿Say: "You will never follow us. Thus God said before."﴾ That is, God promised the people of al-Hudaybiyah before your request to go out with them. ﴿Then they will say, "No, you envy us."﴾ That is, that we would share you in the spoils. ﴿Rather, they did not understand except a little﴾ That is, the matter is not as they claim, but they have no understanding [[In T, A: "Because they are enemies to them."]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 48, verse 16–17:

The commentators differed concerning these people who will be called upon, who possess great military might, into several opinions:

The first: they are Hawazin. This was related by Shu'bah from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, or both of them [In one manuscript: "Hawazin, said by Ikrimah"]. Hushaym also related it from Abu Bishr, from both of them. Qatadah, in one narration from him, also holds this view.

The second: they are Thaqif, said by al-Dahhak.

The third: they are Banu Hanifah, said by Juwaybir. Muhammad ibn Ishaq related it from al-Zuhri, and the like of it is reported from Sa'id and Ikrimah.

The fourth: they are the people of Persia. This was related by Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, and 'Ata', Mujahid, and Ikrimah, in one of the narrations from him, also hold this view.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: they are the Romans. From Ibn Abi Layla, 'Ata', al-Hasan, and Qatadah: they are Persia and the Romans. From Mujahid: they are the people of idols. And from him also: they are men of great might, and he did not specify a particular group. Ibn Juraij holds this view, and it is the preference of Ibn Jarir.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Ashajj related to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hasan al-Qawariri related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding His saying: ﴿You will be called to a people of great might﴾, he said: "Those have not yet come."

And my father related to us, Ibn Abi Umar related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah regarding His saying: ﴿You will be called to a people of great might﴾, he said: "They are the ones who come out (al-Barizun)."

He said: And Sufyan related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "The Hour will not come until you fight a people with small eyes, flat noses, whose faces are like hammered shields." Sufyan said: "They are the Turks" [Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (no. 19199) and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (no. 2929) related it through Sufyan from al-Zuhri with its chain: "The Hour will not come until you fight a people whose faces are as if they were hammered shields."
