'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: ﴿and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."

Qatadah said: ﴿and He made them adhere to the word of righteousness﴾: "There is no deity except Allah."

﴿and they were more worthy of it and deserving of it﴾: the Muslims were more worthy of it, and they were its people.

﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾, meaning He knows who deserves good and who deserves evil.

Al-Nasa'i said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Shababah ibn Sawwar narrated to us, from Abu Razin, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Ala' ibn Zabr, from Busr ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from Abu Idris, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he used to recite: ﴿When those who disbelieved put into their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of ignorance﴾ [al-Fath: 26], "and if you had been zealous as they were zealous, the Sacred Mosque would have been corrupted." This reached 'Umar, who rebuked him harshly, and said: "You know that I used to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he would teach me what Allah had taught him." Ubayy said: "No, you are a man who has knowledge and the Qur'an. So recite, and teach what Allah and His Messenger have taught you." [[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11505).]]

This is the mention of the hadiths related about the story of al-Hudaybiyyah and the story of the treaty:

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, intending to visit the House, not intending fighting. He led with him seventy camels for the offering, and the people were seven hundred men, and each camel was for ten. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out until, when he was at 'Usfan, Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Ka'bi [[In T: "Bishr ibn Ka'b al-Kalbi."]] met him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are Quraysh, who have heard of your march, and have gone out with them the mothers of young camels (al-'awdh al-mataafil), wearing leopard skins, vowing to Allah that they will never let you enter them by force. And this is Khalid ibn al-Walid with their cavalry, whom they have sent forward to Kura' al-Ghamim." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to Quraysh! War has devoured them. What is wrong with them if they leave me between myself and the rest of the people? If they kill me, that is what they wanted, and if Allah makes me victorious over them, they will enter Islam while they are numerous, and if they do not do so, they will fight while they have strength. What does Quraysh think? By Allah, I will not cease to strive against them for that with which Allah sent me, until Allah makes me victorious or this affair is finished." Then he commanded the people, and they took the right-hand way through the midst of the salt-marsh (al-hamd) on a path that would bring them out onto the pass of al-Murar and al-Hudaybiyyah, from the lower part of Makkah. He said: So he led the army along that path. When the horsemen of Quraysh saw the dust of the army, having deviated from their route, they rode back quickly to Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went forward until, when he took the pass of al-Murar, his she-camel knelt down. The people said: "She has become stubborn." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "She has not become stubborn, nor is that her habit, but the one who stopped the elephant from Makkah has stopped her. By Allah, Quraysh will not call me today to any arrangement in which they ask me to keep the ties of kinship, except that I will give it to them." Then he said to the people: "Dismount." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is no water in the valley for the people to alight at." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took out an arrow from his quiver and gave it to a man of his companions, who descended into one of the wells there and planted it in it, and the water gushed forth until the people drew water from it to their fill. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reassured, Budayl ibn Warqa' came with men from Khuza'ah, and he said to them what he had said to Bishr ibn Sufyan. They returned to Quraysh and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, you are hastening against Muhammad, but Muhammad did not come to fight. He only came as a visitor to this House, honouring its sanctity." But they accused them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of al-Zuhri: Khuza'ah were the trusted confidants of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), both their polytheists and their Muslims. They concealed nothing from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that happened in Makkah. The Quraysh said: "Even if he has come only for that, by Allah, he will never enter it against us by force, and the Arabs will not speak of it." Then they sent Mikraz ibn Hafs, of the Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ay, to him. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him, he said: "This is a treacherous man." When he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke to him in much the same way he had spoken to his companions. Then he returned to the Quraysh and informed them of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to him.

They then sent al-Hulays ibn 'Alqamah al-Kinani, who was at that time the chief of the Ahabish (a confederation of tribes allied with Quraysh). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him, he said: "This is one of a people who revere their deities, so bring the sacrificial animals before him." So they brought the sacrificial animals before him. When he saw the animals coming toward him from the valley floor, wearing their garlands, their hides chafed from the long delay in reaching their place of sacrifice, he turned back without reaching the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), out of reverence for what he had seen. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, I have seen what must not be prevented: the sacrificial animals, garlanded, their hides worn from the long detention away from their place of sacrifice." They said: "Sit down, you are only a Bedouin with no knowledge."

Then they sent 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, I have seen what you suffer from those you send to Muhammad when they come to him, of reproach and harsh words. You know that you are my fathers and I am your son. I have heard of what has befallen you, so I gathered those of my people who obeyed me, and came to you so that I might share your plight with my own self." They said: "You have spoken truly; you are not suspected by us." So he went out until he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and sat before him. He said: "O Muhammad, you have gathered the rabble of people and then brought them to your own kin to destroy them. Indeed, Quraysh has come out with the suckling mothers of their young, wearing leopard skins, swearing by Allah that they will never let you enter them by force. By Allah, I see these people abandoning you tomorrow."

He said: Abu Bakr was sitting behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat! Would we abandon him?!" 'Urwah said: "Who is this, O Muhammad?" He said: "This is the son of Abu Quhafah." 'Urwah said: "By Allah, were it not for a favor you once did me, I would have repaid you for it, but this is in return for that." Then he reached out and took hold of the beard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah was standing over the head of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wearing iron armor. He said: so he struck his hand and said: "Take your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), before it does not reach you." 'Urwah said: "Woe to you! How coarse and harsh you are!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled. 'Urwah said: "Who is this, O Muhammad?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is your nephew, al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah." 'Urwah said: "You treacherous one! Did you not wash your private parts only yesterday?!" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke to him in the same manner he had spoken to his companions, and informed him that he had not come seeking war. He said: 'Urwah then rose from the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) having seen how his companions treated him: whenever he performed ablution, they rushed to collect the water he used; whenever he spat, they rushed to catch it; and whenever a hair fell from him, they took it.

He returned to Quraysh and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, I have gone to Chosroes in his kingdom, I have gone to Caesar and the Negus in their kingdoms, and by Allah, I have never seen a king among his companions like Muhammad among his. I have seen a people who will never abandon him for anything, so consider your opinion."

He said: Before this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent Khirash ibn Umayyah al-Khuza'i to Makkah, mounted on his camel called "al-Tha'lab." When he entered Makkah, the Quraysh hamstrung the camel and wanted to kill Khirash, but the Ahabish prevented them, until he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned 'Umar to send him to Makkah. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I fear for myself at the hands of Quraysh, and there is no one of the Banu 'Adi in Makkah to protect me, and Quraysh knows my enmity toward them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honored than I: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Uthman and sent him to Quraysh to inform them that he had not come to fight anyone, but had come only as a visitor to this House, honoring its sanctity.

'Uthman set out until he reached Makkah, where Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As met him. He dismounted from his mount, carried him before himself, rode behind him, and gave him protection until he delivered the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). 'Uthman went to Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Quraysh and conveyed to them what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent him with. They said to 'Uthman: "If you wish to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate it." He said: "I will not do so until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulates it." He said: Quraysh held him back with them. He said: And news reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that 'Uthman had been killed.

Muhammad said: al-Zuhri related to me that Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and said: "Go to Muhammad and make peace with him, but there must be no term in the treaty except that he withdraws from us this year. By Allah, the Arabs must never say that he entered it against us by force." Suhayl ibn 'Amr came to him, and when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him, he said: "The people have wanted peace since they sent this man." When he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they spoke together and prolonged their discussion, and they went back and forth until the peace was concluded between them. When the matter was settled and only the writing of the document remained, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab leapt up and went to Abu Bakr. He said: "O Abu Bakr, is he not the Messenger of Allah? Are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?" Abu Bakr said: "O 'Umar, hold fast to his stirrup wherever he is, for I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah." Then 'Umar said: "And I bear witness." Then he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?" He said: "I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger; I will never oppose His command, and He will never abandon me." Then 'Umar said: "I continued to fast, pray, give charity, and free slaves because of what I did, out of fear of the words I spoke that day, until I hoped it would be good."

He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "Write: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.'" Suhayl ibn 'Amr said: "I do not recognize this. Rather, write: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Write: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" Then he said: "This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to with Suhayl ibn 'Amr." Suhayl ibn 'Amr said: "If I had testified that you are the Messenger of Allah, I would not have fought you. Rather, write: 'This is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah and Suhayl ibn 'Amr have agreed upon, to suspend war for ten years, during which people will be secure and refrain from harming one another, on the condition that whoever comes to the Messenger of Allah from his companions without the permission of his guardian, he will be returned to them; and whoever comes to Quraysh from those with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they will not return him to him. Between us is a sealed chest, there shall be no secret theft and no betrayal.'" It was also among their conditions when they wrote the document that whoever wished to enter the covenant and pact of Muhammad could do so, and whoever wished to enter the covenant and pact of Quraysh could do so. Then Khuza'ah sprang up and said: "We are in the covenant and pact of the Messenger of Allah." And Banu Bakr sprang up and said: "We are in the covenant and pact of Quraysh." And [the condition was] that you withdraw from us this year and not enter Makkah against us; and that when the coming year arrives, we will withdraw from you, and you may enter it with your companions, and remain there three days, with the arms of a rider, not entering with anything but swords in their sheaths.

While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was writing the document, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr came to him in iron shackles, having escaped to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah had set out, not doubting in the conquest, because of a dream the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had seen. When they saw what they saw of the peace and the return, and what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had taken upon himself, a great distress entered the people, until they nearly perished. When Suhayl saw Abu Jandal, he rose to him, struck his face, and said: "O Muhammad, the agreement between me and you was concluded before this one came to you." He said: "You have spoken truly." Suhayl rose to him and seized him by his collar. He said: Abu Jandal cried out at the top of his voice: "O assembly of Muslims, will you return me to the people of polytheism so that they tempt me in my religion?" He said: This increased the people's distress beyond what they already bore. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Jandal, be patient and seek your reward, for Allah will surely make for you and for those weak ones with you a relief and a way out. We have concluded between us and these people a peace, and we have given them our word on that, and they have given us their word on it, and we will not betray them."

He said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab sprang up and began walking beside Abu Jandal, saying: "Be patient, Abu Jandal, for they are only polytheists, and the blood of any one of them is the blood of a dog." He said: And he brought the hilt of the sword close to him. He said: He [Umar] said: "I hoped he would take the sword and strike his father with it." He said: But the man was reluctant regarding his father. He said: The agreement was carried through. When they had finished the document, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was praying in the Sacred Precinct, while he was outside it in the open area, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood and said: "O people, sacrifice and shave your heads." He said: No one stood up. He said: He repeated it, and still no man stood, until he repeated it a third time, and still no man stood.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned and entered upon Umm Salamah, and said: "O Umm Salamah, what is the matter with the people?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, they have been overcome by what you have seen. Do not speak to any of them, but go to your sacrificial animal, slaughter it, and shave your head. If you do that, the people will do the same." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out without speaking to anyone until he came to his sacrificial animal and slaughtered it. Then he sat down and had his head shaved. He said: So the people rose, slaughtering and shaving. He said: Until, when he was between Makkah and Madinah, in the middle of the road, Surat al-Fath was revealed.

Thus Ahmad related it through this chain, and thus Yunus ibn Bukayr and Ziyad al-Bakka'i related it from Ibn Ishaq, in similar wording (al-Musnad 4/323 and al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham 2/316), and in it there is some strangeness. It was also related from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, in similar wording (Ahmad related it in his Musnad 4/328 through 'Abd al-Razzaq). He differed from him in some points. Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, also related it in his Sahih, giving a good and extended account with excellent additions. He said in the Book of Conditions of his Sahih:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 48, verses 25–26 (part 3 of 4):

'Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us: al-Zuhri informed me: 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me, on the authority of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, each of whom confirmed the other's report. They both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out during the time of al-Hudaybiyyah with about fourteen hundred of his Companions. When he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, he garlanded the sacrificial animal (al-hady) and marked it, and he entered the state of ihram (ritual consecration) for 'Umrah (the lesser pilgrimage) from there. He sent a scout of his from Khuza'ah and proceeded until, when he was at Ghadir al-Ashtat, his scout came to him and said: "Quraysh have gathered large forces against you. They have also gathered the Ahabish (allied tribes), and they will fight you, block you, and prevent you."

He said: "Give me your counsel, O people. Do you think we should turn against their dependants and offspring, those who want to bar us from the House?" In another version: "Do you think we should turn against the offspring of those who assisted them? If they come to us, Allah will have cut off a limb of the polytheists; and if they do not, we will have left them grieved." In another version: "If they stay, they will stay wronged, exhausted, and defeated; and if they escape, it will be a limb that Allah has cut off. Or do you think we should head for the House, and whoever bars us from it, we fight him?"

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) [the phrase is supplied from another manuscript] said: "O Messenger of Allah, you set out intending this House, not wanting to kill anyone or to wage war. So head towards it, and whoever bars us from it, we will fight him." In another version, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Allah and His Messenger know that we came as pilgrims and did not come to fight anyone. But whoever stands between us and the House, we will fight him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then proceed," and in another version: "Then go on in the name of Allah."

When they were at some part of the way, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Khalid ibn al-Walid is in the vanguard of Quraysh's cavalry, so take the right-hand route." By Allah, Khalid did not perceive them until he suddenly saw the dust of the army, so he hurried off at a gallop to warn Quraysh. The Prophet (ﷺ) continued until, when he was at the mountain pass through which they would descend upon them, his she-camel knelt down with him. The people said: "Halt! Halt!" but she kept insisting, so they said: "al-Qaswa has become stubborn, al-Qaswa has become stubborn!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "al-Qaswa has not become stubborn, nor is that her habit, but the One who restrained the elephant has restrained her." Then he said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, they will not ask me for any arrangement in which they honour the sacred things of Allah without my granting it to them." Then he urged her on and she sprang up. He turned away from them until he halted at the farthest end of al-Hudaybiyyah, at a small spring with little water, from which people drew water only in small trickles. The people soon drained it completely, and they complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of thirst. He drew an arrow from his quiver and then ordered them to place it in the spring. By Allah, the water kept gushing up for them until they left it.

While they were in this state, Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i came with a group of his people from Khuza'ah, who were the trusted confidants (of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)) among the people of Tihamah. He said: "I left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy and 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy encamped at the watering places of al-Hudaybiyyah, with them the milch camels with their young, and they will fight you and bar you from the House." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We have not come to fight anyone, but we have come as pilgrims. Quraysh have been worn down by war and it has harmed them. If they wish, we will make a truce with them for a period and they will leave me and the people to deal with one another. If I prevail, they may enter into what the people have entered into, if they wish; otherwise they will have rested. And if they refuse, by He in whose hand is my soul, I will fight them for this cause of mine until my neck is severed, and Allah will surely make His command prevail."

Budayl said: "I will convey to them what you say." He set off and came to Quraysh and said: "We have come from this man, and we heard him say something. If you wish, we will present it to you." Their foolish ones said: "We have no need for you to tell us anything about him." But their men of judgement said: "Relate what you heard him say." He said: "I heard him say such and such," and he related to them what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said.

Then 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud stood up and said: "O people, are you not the father?" They said: "Yes." He said: "And am I not the son?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Do you suspect me?" They said: "No." He said: "Do you not know that I called upon the people of 'Ukaz, and when they hung back from me, I brought you my family, my children, and those who obeyed me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "This man has presented you with a proposal of right guidance, so accept it, and let me go to him." They said: "Go to him."

So he came to him and began speaking with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him something similar to what he had said to Budayl ibn Warqa'. 'Urwah then said: "O Muhammad, tell me: if you uproot the affair of your own people, have you ever heard of anyone among the Arabs who destroyed his own kin before you? And if the other outcome occurs, then by Allah, I see faces, and I see a motley crowd of people who are likely to flee and abandon you." Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat! Would we flee and abandon him?!" He (Urwah) said: "Who is this?" They said: "Abu Bakr." He said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favour you once did me, which I have not yet repaid, I would have answered you."

He continued speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), and every time he spoke to him he would take hold of his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (may Allah be pleased with him) was standing over the head of the Prophet (ﷺ) with a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever 'Urwah reached out his hand toward the beard of the Prophet (ﷺ), he would strike his hand with the scabbard of the sword and say to him: "Keep your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." 'Urwah raised his head and said: "Who is this?" He said: "Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah." He said: "You treacherous one! Am I not striving to atone for your treachery?" Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah had accompanied a people in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period), killed them, and taken their property; then he came and embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for Islam, we accept it; but as for the wealth, I have no share in it at all."

Then 'Urwah began to look at the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) with his eyes. He said: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never spat a mucus except that it fell into the palm of one of them, who rubbed it over his face and skin. If he ordered them, they rushed to carry out his command; when he performed ablution, they almost fought over his ablution water; and when he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and they did not stare at him intently, out of reverence for him." Then 'Urwah returned to his companions and said: "O people, by Allah, I have visited kings: I have visited Chosroes, Caesar, and the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whom his companions revere as the Companions of Muhammad revere Muhammad. By Allah, if he spits a mucus, it falls into the palm of one of them, who rubs it over his face and skin; if he orders them, they rush to carry out his command; if he performs ablution, they almost fight over his ablution water; if he speaks, they lower their voices in his presence, and they do not stare at him intently out of reverence for him. Indeed, he has presented you with a proposal of right guidance, so accept it."

A man from them, from the Banu Kinanah, said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he approached the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who honour the sacrificial camels, so bring the camels out for him." The camels were brought out for him, and the people came to meet him, chanting the talbiyah (the call of "Labbayka"). When he saw this, he said: "Glory be to Allah! It is not right that these people be barred from the House." When he returned to his companions, he said: "I have seen the camels garlanded and marked, and I do not think they should be barred from the House."

Then a man from them, called Mikraz ibn Hafs, stood up and said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he approached them, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is Mikraz ibn Hafs, and he is a wicked man." He began speaking with the Prophet (ﷺ), and while he was speaking with him, Suhayl ibn 'Amr came.

Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me, on the authority of 'Ikrimah, that when Suhayl ibn 'Amr came, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Your affair has become easy for you."

Ma'mar said: al-Zuhri said in his narration: Suhayl ibn 'Amr came and said: "Come, let us write a document between us and you." So the Prophet (ﷺ) summoned the scribe, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Suhayl said: "As for 'the Most Merciful' (al-Rahman), by Allah, I do not know what it is. But write: 'In Your name, O Allah,' as you used to write." The Muslims said: "By Allah, we will not write it except as 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.'" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Write: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" Then he said: "This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to." Suhayl said: "By Allah, if we knew you to be the Messenger of Allah, we would not have barred you from the House nor fought you. But write: 'Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah.'" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I am indeed the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me. Write: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah." Al-Zuhri said: This was in accordance with his saying: "By Allah, they will not ask me for any arrangement in which they honour the sacred things of Allah without my granting it to them."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "On condition that you leave us and the House, so that we may circumambulate it." Suhayl said: "By Allah, the Arabs must not say that we were coerced under pressure. But that will be in the coming year." So he wrote it. Suhayl said: "And on condition that no man from us comes to you, even if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us." The Muslims said: "Glory be to Allah! How can he be returned to the polytheists when he has come as a Muslim?!" While they were in this state, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn 'Amr came, dragging his feet in his shackles, having emerged from the lower part of Makkah, until he threw himself among the Muslims. Suhayl said: "O Muhammad, this is the first person I require you to return to me under this agreement." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We have not yet finalised the document." He said: "By Allah, then I will never make peace with you over anything at all." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Then permit him for me." He said: "I will not permit that for you." He said: "Yes, do so." He said: "I will not do so." Mikraz said: "Yes, we have permitted him for you." Abu Jandal said: "O assembly of Muslims, am I to be returned to the polytheists when I have come as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered?" He had been tortured severely for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I came to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Are you not truly the Prophet of Allah?' He (ﷺ) said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Are we not upon the truth while our enemy is upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?' He said: 'I am the Messenger of Allah, and I do not disobey Him, and He is my helper.' I said: 'Did you not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?' He said: 'Yes. Did I tell you that we would come to it this year?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.'"

He said: "So I went to Abu Bakr and said: 'O Abu Bakr, is this not truly the Prophet of Allah?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Are we not upon the truth while our enemy is upon falsehood?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?' He said: 'O man, he is the Messenger of Allah, and he does not disobey his Lord, and He is his helper. So hold fast to his stirrup, for by Allah, he is upon the truth.' I said: 'Did he not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Did he tell you that you would come to it this year?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.'"

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Fath (48), verses 25–26 (part 4 of 4):

Al-Zuhri said: Umar said: "So I did certain deeds for that." He said: "When [the Prophet] had finished with the matter of the document, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: 'Get up, sacrifice, then shave your heads.'" [In manuscript T: "the Prophet".] He said: "By Allah, not one man among them got up, until he said that three times!! When none of them got up, he entered upon Umm Salamah and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah said to him: 'O Prophet of Allah, do you want that? Go out, and do not speak a single word to any of them until you sacrifice your camel and call your barber, and he shaves you.' So he went out and did not speak to any of them until he had done that: he sacrificed his camel and called his barber, and he shaved him. When they saw that, they got up and sacrificed, and they began shaving one another, until some of them nearly killed one another out of grief. Then believing women came to him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ until: ﴿the disbelieving women [as wives]﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 10]. So Umar divorced two wives who had been his while they were polytheists that day; Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married one of them, and Safwan ibn Umayyah married the other. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) returned to Medina, and Abu Basir, a man of Quraysh, came to him while he was a Muslim. They sent two men in pursuit of him, saying: 'The covenant that you made for us [must be kept].' So he handed him over to the two men, and they set out with him until they reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, where they stopped to eat dates they had with them. Abu Basir said to one of the two men: 'By Allah, I see that your sword, O so-and-so, is fine.' The other drew it and said: 'Indeed, by Allah, it is very fine. I have tested it, and tested it again.' Abu Basir said: 'Show me, let me look at it.' So he gave it to him, and he struck him until he died, and the other fled until he reached Medina. He entered the mosque running. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he saw him, said: 'This man has seen something frightening.' When he reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: 'By Allah, my companion has been killed, and I am about to be killed.' Then Abu Basir came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, Allah has fulfilled your covenant. You returned me to them, then Allah saved me from them.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Woe to his mother, he is a war-kindler! If only he had someone with him!' When he heard that, he understood that the Prophet would return him to them, so he went out until he reached the coast of the sea." He said: "Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl also escaped from them and joined Abu Basir. No man of Quraysh who had embraced Islam went out without joining Abu Basir, until a band of them had gathered. By Allah, they did not hear of a caravan that Quraysh had sent to Syria without intercepting it, killing them and taking their property. So Quraysh sent to the Prophet (ﷺ), appealing to him by Allah and by the ties of kinship, to send for them, promising: 'Whoever comes to him from them is safe.' The Prophet (ﷺ) sent for them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah﴾ until: ﴿the zealotry of the Days of Ignorance﴾. Their zealotry was that they did not acknowledge that he was the Messenger of Allah, and did not acknowledge [the phrase] 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate', and they barred them from the House."

This is how al-Bukhari transmitted it here. He also transmitted it in the Tafsir chapter, in the chapter on the Umrah of Hudaybiyyah, in the chapter on Hajj, and elsewhere, through the narrations of Ma'mar and Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, both from al-Zuhri, with this chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4180.] In some places it occurs as: from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from Marwan and al-Miswar ibn [Makhramah] [addition from manuscript M], from men among the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), with the same content. [Al-Bukhari in his Sahih, at the beginning of the Conditions, no. 2711.] This is more likely, and Allah knows best. He did not transmit it in a fuller form than this, and there are differences between it and the account of Ibn Ishaq in various places. There are benefits there that should be added to what is here, which is why we have cited that narration and this one. Allah is the One sought for help, and in Him is reliance, and there is no power nor strength except with Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

Al-Bukhari said in the Tafsir: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Sulami narrated to us: Ya'la narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Siyah narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: I came to Abu Wa'il to ask him, and he said: "We were at Siffin, and a man said: 'Have you not seen those who call to the Book of Allah?' 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: 'Yes.' Sahl ibn Hunayf said: 'Accuse yourselves, for we saw ourselves on the day of Hudaybiyyah' — meaning the peace treaty that was between the Prophet (ﷺ) and the polytheists — 'and if we had seen fighting, we would have fought. Then Umar came and said: 'Are we not upon the truth and they upon falsehood? Are not our slain in Paradise and their slain in the Fire?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then why do we give the humiliation in our religion, and return while Allah has not yet judged between us?' He said: 'O son of al-Khattab, I am the Messenger of Allah, and Allah will never abandon me, ever.' So he returned angry, and could not be patient until he came to Abu Bakr and said: 'O Abu Bakr, are we not upon the truth and they upon falsehood?' He said: 'O son of al-Khattab, he is the Messenger of Allah, and Allah will never abandon him, ever.' Then Surah al-Fath was revealed."" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4844.]

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in other places, and Muslim and al-Nasa'i through other chains from Abu Wa'il Sufyan [In manuscript H: "Shaqiq"] ibn Salamah, from Sahl [In manuscript M: "Sahl"] ibn Hunayf, with the same content. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 3181, 7308, 4189, 3182; Sahih Muslim, no. 1785; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11504.] In some of its wording: "O people, accuse your opinion, for I saw myself on the day of Abu Jandal, and if I could reverse the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) decision, I would have reversed it." In one narration: "Then Surah al-Fath was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Umar ibn al-Khattab and recited it to him."

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that Quraysh made peace with the Prophet (ﷺ), and among them was Suhayl ibn 'Amr. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Ali: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." Suhayl said: "We do not know what 'In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate' is. Rather, write what we recognize: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" He said: "Write: From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah." He said: "If we knew that you are the Messenger of Allah, we would have followed you. Rather, write: your name and your father's name." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Write: From Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah." They stipulated to the Prophet (ﷺ) that whoever comes to you from us, we will not return him to you, and whoever comes to us from you, you must return him to us. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you write this?" He said: "Yes, for whoever among us goes to them, Allah will keep him far away." Muslim narrated it through the narration of Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same content. [Musnad, 3/268; Sahih Muslim, no. 1784.]

Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: Simak narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When the Harurites [Kharijites] came out, they withdrew, and I said to them: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a treaty with the polytheists at Hudaybiyyah, and he said to 'Ali: "Write, O 'Ali: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon."' They said: 'If we knew that you are the Messenger of Allah, we would not have fought you.' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Erase it, O 'Ali. O Allah, You know that I am Your Messenger. Erase it, O 'Ali, and write: This is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah has agreed upon.' By Allah, the Messenger of Allah is better than 'Ali, and he erased himself, and his erasing that did not erase him from prophethood. Did I bring this out [as an argument]?" They said: "Yes."

Abu Dawud narrated it through the narration of 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar al-Yamami, with similar wording. [Musnad, 1/342; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4037.]

Ahmad also narrated, from Yahya ibn Adam: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed seventy camels at Hudaybiyyah, among them a camel belonging to Abu Jahl. When they were prevented from the House, [the camels] cried out as a mother cries out for her young." [Musnad, 1/314.]

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had been shown in a dream that he entered Makkah and circumambulated the House, and he told his Companions of this while he was in Madinah. When they set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, a group of them did not doubt that this dream would be fulfilled that very year. When what happened in the matter of the treaty (al-sulh) occurred, and they returned that year on the condition that they would come back the following year, something of this lingered in the hearts of some of the Companions. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, asked about it, and among what he said to him was: "Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes. Did I tell you that you would come to it this year?" He said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, also answered in the same way, step for step (hadhw al-qudhdhah bi-l-qudhdhah).

For this reason, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision with truth. You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security﴾. This "if Allah wills" is for confirming and emphasising the report, and it is not at all an exception (istithna'). And His saying ﴿in security﴾ means: during your entry.

His saying ﴿with your heads shaved or your hair cut short﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) that is anticipated (muqaddarah), because at the time of their entry they were not shaving or cutting their hair while in the state of ihram; rather, this happened afterwards. Some of them shaved their heads and some cut their hair short. It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shave." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of God?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shave." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of God?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shave." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of God?" He said, on the third or fourth time: "And those who cut short." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1727, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1301, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.)

* *

His saying ﴿you fear not﴾ is a circumstantial clause that reinforces the meaning. Thus He affirmed security for them at the time of entry, and negated fear from them while they remained in the city, fearing no one.

This was the Umrat al-Qada' (the 'umrah of making up), in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the year seven (AH). When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from al-Hudaybiyah in Dhu al-Qa'dah, he went back to Madinah and stayed there through Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram. He set out in Safar towards Khaybar, and Allah granted him its conquest, part of it by force ('anwatan) and part by treaty (sulhan). It is a great region, abundant in palm trees and crops. He employed the Jews who were in it upon the land on a share of the produce (al-shatr), and he divided it among the people of al-Hudaybiyah alone. No one else witnessed it except those who came from Abyssinia (al-Habashah): Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and his companions, and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and his companions. None of them was absent. Ibn Zayd said: "Except Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, as is established in its proper place." Then he returned to Madinah.

When it was Dhu al-Qa'dah of the year seven, he set out for Makkah as a performer of 'umrah, he and the people of al-Hudaybiyah. He assumed ihram from Dhu al-Hulayfah and brought along the sacrificial animals (al-hady). It was said that there were sixty camels (badanah). He recited the talbiyah, and his Companions also recited the talbiyah as they walked.

When he was near Marr al-Zahran, he sent Muhammad ibn Maslamah ahead with horses and weapons. When the polytheists saw him, they were struck with terrible fear, and they thought that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was going to attack them, and that he had broken the agreement between them concerning the cessation of fighting for ten years. They went and informed the people of Makkah. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) arrived and halted at Marr al-Zahran, from where he could see the boundary markers of the Haram, he sent the weapons—bows, arrows and spears—to Batn Yajaj, and he went to Makkah with his sword sheathed in its scabbard, as he had stipulated with them. When he was midway along the road, Quraysh sent Mikraz ibn Hafs, who said: "O Muhammad, we did not know you to break the covenant." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "You entered upon us with weapons, bows and spears." He (ﷺ) said: "That did not happen, and we have sent them to Yajaj." He said: "By this we knew you: righteousness and fulfilment."

The leaders of the disbelievers came out of Makkah so that they would not have to look at the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions, out of rage and fury. As for the rest of the people of Makkah, men, women and children, they sat in the streets and on the rooftops, looking at the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions. He, peace and blessings be upon him, entered with his Companions before him reciting the talbiyah, and the sacrificial animals had been sent ahead to Dhu Tuwa. He was riding his she-camel al-Qaswa', the one he had ridden on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, and Abd Allah ibn Rawahah al-Ansari was holding the reins of the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) she-camel, leading her, and he was saying:

"In the name of the One besides whom there is no religion but His,
in the name of the One whose Messenger is Muhammad.

His Companions said: "If we slaughtered our mounts, ate their meat and drank their broth, we would arrive tomorrow when we enter upon the people with our strength intact." He said: "Do not do that, but gather for me some of your provisions." They gathered for him, spread out the leather sheets (al-anta'), and they ate until they had left some, and each one of them stuffed his saddlebag. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came until he entered the mosque, while Quraysh were sitting near the Hijr. He put his cloak under his right arm and threw its ends over his left shoulder (idtiba'), then said: "May the people not see in you any weakness (ghamirah)." He touched the corner (al-rukn), then performed the ramal (a quick, bouncing gait), until when he had gone behind the Yemeni corner, he walked to the Black Stone. His saying: ﴿So He knew what you did not know, and He appointed besides that a near victory﴾: that is, Allah the Exalted knew the wisdom (*khiyarah*) and the benefit in turning you away from Makkah and preventing your entry into it in that year, which you did not know. ﴿He appointed besides that﴾: that is, before your entry which you were promised in the vision of the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿A near victory﴾: this is the treaty that was between you and your enemies among the polytheists.

Then Allah the Exalted said, giving good news to the believers of the Messenger's (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) victory over his enemy and over all the rest of the people of the earth: ﴿He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾: that is, with beneficial knowledge and righteous action. For the Sharia (divine law) comprises two things: knowledge and action. Sharia knowledge is sound, and Sharia action is accepted; its reports are true and its rulings are just. ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾: that is, over the adherents of all religions among all the people of the earth, Arabs and non-Arabs, the people of the (revealed) religions (*Millliyyin*) and the polytheists. [[In manuscript A: "Muslims."]] ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Witness﴾: that is, that He is His Messenger, and He is his helper.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had been shown in a dream that he entered Makkah and circumambulated the House, and he told his Companions of this while he was in Madinah. When they set out in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, a group of them did not doubt that this dream would be fulfilled that very year. When what happened in the matter of the treaty (al-sulh) occurred, and they returned that year on the condition that they would come back the following year, something of this lingered in the hearts of some of the Companions. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, asked about it, and among what he said to him was: "Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes. Did I tell you that you would come to it this year?" He said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, also answered in the same way, step for step (hadhw al-qudhdhah bi-l-qudhdhah).

For this reason, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision with truth. You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security﴾. This "if Allah wills" is for confirming and emphasising the report, and it is not at all an exception (istithna'). And His saying ﴿in security﴾ means: during your entry.

His saying ﴿with your heads shaved or your hair cut short﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) that is anticipated (muqaddarah), because at the time of their entry they were not shaving or cutting their hair while in the state of ihram; rather, this happened afterwards. Some of them shaved their heads and some cut their hair short. It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shave." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of God?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shave." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of God?" He said: "May Allah have mercy on those who shave." They said: "And those who cut short, O Messenger of God?" He said, on the third or fourth time: "And those who cut short." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1727, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1301, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.)

His saying ﴿you fear not﴾ is a circumstantial clause that reinforces the meaning. Thus He affirmed security for them at the time of entry, and negated fear from them while they remained in the city, fearing no one.

This was the Umrat al-Qada' (the 'umrah of making up), in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the year seven (AH). When the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from al-Hudaybiyah in Dhu al-Qa'dah, he went back to Madinah and stayed there through Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram. He set out in Safar towards Khaybar, and Allah granted him its conquest, part of it by force ('anwatan) and part by treaty (sulhan). It is a great region, abundant in palm trees and crops. He employed the Jews who were in it upon the land on a share of the produce (al-shatr), and he divided it among the people of al-Hudaybiyah alone. No one else witnessed it except those who came from Abyssinia (al-Habashah): Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and his companions, and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and his companions. None of them was absent. Ibn Zayd said: "Except Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, as is established in its proper place." Then he returned to Madinah.

When it was Dhu al-Qa'dah of the year seven, he set out for Makkah as a performer of 'umrah, he and the people of al-Hudaybiyah. He assumed ihram from Dhu al-Hulayfah and brought along the sacrificial animals (al-hady). It was said that there were sixty camels (badanah). He recited the talbiyah, and his Companions also recited the talbiyah as they walked.

When he was near Marr al-Zahran, he sent Muhammad ibn Maslamah ahead with horses and weapons. When the polytheists saw him, they were struck with terrible fear, and they thought that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was going to attack them, and that he had broken the agreement between them concerning the cessation of fighting for ten years. They went and informed the people of Makkah. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) arrived and halted at Marr al-Zahran, from where he could see the boundary markers of the Haram, he sent the weapons—bows, arrows and spears—to Batn Yajaj, and he went to Makkah with his sword sheathed in its scabbard, as he had stipulated with them. When he was midway along the road, Quraysh sent Mikraz ibn Hafs, who said: "O Muhammad, we did not know you to break the covenant." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "You entered upon us with weapons, bows and spears." He (ﷺ) said: "That did not happen, and we have sent them to Yajaj." He said: "By this we knew you: righteousness and fulfilment."

The leaders of the disbelievers came out of Makkah so that they would not have to look at the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions, out of rage and fury. As for the rest of the people of Makkah, men, women and children, they sat in the streets and on the rooftops, looking at the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions. He, peace and blessings be upon him, entered with his Companions before him reciting the talbiyah, and the sacrificial animals had been sent ahead to Dhu Tuwa. He was riding his she-camel al-Qaswa', the one he had ridden on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, and Abd Allah ibn Rawahah al-Ansari was holding the reins of the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) she-camel, leading her, and he was saying:

in the name of the One whose Messenger is Muhammad.
Make way, sons of the disbelievers, from His path!
Today we strike you over its interpretation,
as we struck you over its revelation,
a blow that removes the skull from its resting place,
and makes the close friend forget his close friend.

Ibn Kathir says, concerning Muhammad (may the blessings of Allah be upon him), that he is truly the Messenger of Allah without any doubt or uncertainty. Allah says: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah﴾. This is a subject and predicate construction, and it includes every beautiful attribute. Then He followed this with praise of his Companions, saying: ﴿And those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾, just as Allah says: ﴿Allah will bring forth a people He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty over the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 54]. This is the attribute of the believers: that each one of them is harsh and fierce against the disbelievers, merciful and kind toward the righteous, stern-faced toward the disbeliever, and smiling and cheerful toward his believing brother, just as Allah says: ﴿O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you, and let them find harshness in you﴾ [At-Tawbah: 123]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, mercy and compassion is like the likeness of a single body: when one of its limbs complains, the rest of the body responds to it with wakefulness and fever." [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3011, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2586, from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him.] And he said: "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part of which strengthens another," and he interlaced his fingers [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 481, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2585, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him]. Both hadiths are in the Sahih.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and approval﴾: He described them with abundance of deeds and abundance of prayer, which is the best of deeds, and described them as sincere in it for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and as seeking great reward with Allah, which is Paradise, encompassing the bounty of Allah, which is abundance of provision for them, and His approval of them, exalted is He, which is greater than the first, as He says: ﴿But approval from Allah is greater﴾ [At-Tawbah: 72].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾: Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Their mark is on their faces﴾ means: the good bearing (al-samt al-hasan).

Mujahid and others said: it means humility and submissiveness.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Husayn al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, from Mujahid regarding ﴿Their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾, he said: it is humility. I said: I used to think it was only this trace on the face. He said: Sometimes it is between the eyes of one who is harder of heart than Pharaoh.

As-Suddi said: Prayer beautifies their faces.

Some of the early scholars said: Whoever prays much at night, his face becomes beautiful by day.

Ibn Majah traced this in his Sunan from Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Talhi, from Thabit ibn Musa, from Sharik, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays much at night, his face becomes beautiful by day." The correct view is that it is a statement of a Companion (mawquf) [Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1333].

Some of them said: Indeed, good deeds have a light in the heart, radiance on the face, abundance in provision, and love in the hearts of people.

Amir al-Mu'minin Uthman said: No one conceals a secret except that Allah brings it out upon the pages of his face and the slips of his tongue.

The point is that what is hidden within the soul appears on the surfaces of the face. So the believer, when his inner self is sound with Allah, Allah makes his outward appearance good to the people, as is narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Whoever sets right his inner self, Allah sets right his outward appearance.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Mahmud ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to us, Hamid ibn Adam al-Marwazi narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah al-Arzami, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Jundab ibn Sufyan al-Bajali, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one conceals a secret except that Allah clothes him in its garment: if it is good, then good, and if it is evil, then evil." Al-Arzami is abandoned (matruk) [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/171); and Hamid ibn Adam is a liar].

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "If one of you were to work inside a solid rock that has no door and no window, his deed would come out for the people, whatever it may be." [al-Musnad (3/28)].

Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan narrated to us: that his father narrated to him from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, good guidance, good bearing, and moderation are one part of twenty-five parts of prophethood." Abu Dawud also narrated it from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Nufayli, from Zuhayr, with the same chain [al-Musnad (1/296); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4776].

So the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) had sincere intentions and good deeds, so whoever looked at them was impressed by their bearing and their guidance.

Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It reached me that the Christians, when they saw the Companions who conquered Syria, would say: "By Allah, these are better than the disciples (al-hawariyyun), as it has reached us." And they spoke the truth in that, for this Ummah is exalted in the earlier scriptures, and the greatest and best of it are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah has honored their mention in the revealed books and in the widely circulated reports. Therefore He said here: ﴿That is their likeness in the Torah﴾; then He said: ﴿And their likeness in the Gospel is like a seed that sends out its shoot, then strengthens it, so it becomes thick and stands on its stalk﴾. ﴿Sent out its shoot﴾ means its offshoots; ﴿strengthened it﴾ means supported it; ﴿became thick﴾ means grew and lengthened; ﴿stood on its stalk, pleasing the sowers﴾. Likewise, the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) supported him, aided him and helped him, so they are with him like the shoot with the seed, ﴿that He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾.

From this verse, Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, in one narration from him, derived the judgment of disbelief against the Rafidah who hate the Companions. He said: Because they enrage them, and whoever enrages the Companions is a disbeliever by this verse. A group of scholars agreed with him on this. The hadiths concerning the virtues of the Companions and the prohibition of harming them are very numerous, and Allah's praise of them and His approval of them is sufficient for them.

Then He said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believed and did righteous deeds among them﴾, where "min" here is for specifying the category, ﴿forgiveness﴾, meaning for their sins, ﴿and a great reward﴾, meaning abundant reward and generous provision. Allah's promise is true and sincere; it is not broken or changed. Whoever follows the footsteps of the Companions is in their rank, and they have the virtue, precedence and perfection in which no one of this Ummah can equal them. May Allah be pleased with them and make them content, and make the Gardens of Paradise their abode, and He has done so.

Muslim said in his Sahih: Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile my Companions. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend gold equal to Uhud, he would not reach a mudd of one of them, nor even half of it" [Sahih Muslim, no. 2540].

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Fath, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
